Q956.t: An imperial grid framed by mountains on two sides
Q956.s: Beijing is laid out like a chessboard: straight avenues, a strict north–south axis and ring roads nested one inside another. Mountains curl around it on the west and north, while the plain opens towards the sea in the south-east. Its name means “northern capital”, and emperors ruled from here for most of the time since the 13th century.
Q956.w: A vast grid on a flat plain, hemmed in by dark mountains to the north and west; at night, rectangular rings of light.
f: The 2nd Ring Road traces the line of the old city walls, which were largely pulled down in the 20th century.
The Grand Canal, almost 1,800 km long, reaches its northern end on Beijing's eastern side.
The Forbidden City, finished in 1420, sits exactly on the city's north–south axis.

q.q: What does the name “Beijing” mean?

Q3630.t: Java's great sprawl, with a scatter of islands offshore
Q3630.s: Jakarta spreads over a flat, hazy plain where Java meets the shallow Java Sea, and the city seems to have no edge — it simply fades into its neighbours. Offshore, the Thousand Islands dot the water like crumbs. On a clear day, volcanic cones rise to the south. The Dutch called it Batavia and ran their East Indies trade from here.
Q3630.w: A huge grey sprawl on Java's north coast, a bay with small islands to the north, volcanoes on the southern horizon.
f: Despite their name, the Thousand Islands off Jakarta number only a little over a hundred.
The Dutch East India Company founded Batavia here in 1619, on the site of the port of Jayakarta.
The old harbour of Sunda Kelapa still hosts wooden pinisi schooners.

q.q: What was Jakarta called under Dutch rule?

Q8686.t: Where the muddy Yangtze finally meets the sea
Q8686.s: Look for brown water turning blue: the Yangtze pours its silt into the East China Sea right beside Shanghai. The city lies flat on the south bank, cut in two by the winding Huangpu River. Out to sea, a hair-thin line runs across the water — a bridge more than 30 km long to an island container port.
Q8686.w: A giant flat city on the south side of the brown Yangtze estuary, with a long, low island in the river mouth.
f: Chongming Island in the Yangtze mouth is built entirely of river silt and is about 80 km long.
Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port since 2010.
The name is usually read as “on the sea” or “upon the sea”.

q.q: Which river winds through the centre of Shanghai?

Q1490.t: A city that fills an entire plain, wrapped round a bay
Q1490.s: Tokyo does not so much end as run out of flat land: buildings cover the Kanto Plain, Japan's largest, from the mountains to the sea. The city wraps around Tokyo Bay, much of whose shore is reclaimed land. On a clear day Fuji's cone stands about 100 km to the south-west. Until 1868 this was Edo, the shoguns' city.
Q1490.w: Continuous city around a wide bay; Fuji's lone cone to the south-west; at night an unbroken carpet of lights.
f: Odaiba is named after cannon batteries built in the bay in 1853–54, after Commodore Perry's ships arrived.
The name Tokyo means “eastern capital”; the emperor moved here from Kyoto in 1868–69.
The Aqua-Line runs out into Tokyo Bay and seems to stop at an island — the rest of the road is a tunnel under the seabed.

q.q: What was Tokyo called before 1868?

Q1156.t: Seven islands stitched into one long peninsula
Q1156.s: Mumbai points south into the Arabian Sea like a thumb. It was once seven separate islands, joined from the 18th century onwards by causeways and landfill into one crowded strip. Harbour water lies to the east, open sea to the west. After dark, look for the bright curve of lights along Back Bay — locals call it the Queen's Necklace.
Q1156.w: A narrow finger of land jutting south into the sea, a wide harbour on its east side, a green forest patch in the north.
f: Portugal handed Bombay to England in 1661 as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry on her marriage to Charles II.
Sanjay Gandhi National Park, a forest with wild leopards, lies inside the city limits.
A sea bridge about 22 km long, opened in 2024, links the city with the mainland across the harbour.

q.q: Mumbai was formed by joining how many islands?

Q1348.t: Former capital of British India on a delta river
Q1348.s: Kolkata stretches along the east bank of the Hooghly, a working arm of the Ganges, with Howrah facing it across the water. Beyond its eastern edge, a patchwork of ponds and marshes quietly cleans the city's wastewater and raises fish. Further south the land dissolves into the channels and mangroves of the Sundarbans. Until 1911, this was the capital of British India.
Q1348.w: A long city on a brown river running north–south; square fish ponds to the east, delta channels to the south.
f: The East Kolkata Wetlands use the city's sewage to feed fish ponds and are a protected Ramsar site.
Kolkata's port lies on the river, well over 100 km from the open sea.
The Sundarbans to the south are the world's largest mangrove forest, shared with Bangladesh.

q.q: Which river flows through Kolkata?

Q3130.t: A drowned valley of blue fingers, open to the Pacific
Q3130.s: Sydney's harbour is a drowned river valley, and from above it looks like a hand of blue fingers reaching deep into the city. Sandstone headlands guard its narrow mouth to the Pacific. South lies Botany Bay, where the airport's runways run out into the water. To the west, the Blue Mountains rise in a haze that really does look blue.
Q3130.w: A deep, branching harbour entering the coast between two headlands; a round bay with runways to the south.
f: The blue haze over the Blue Mountains comes from oils evaporating from eucalyptus leaves.
James Cook landed at Botany Bay in 1770; the First Fleet settled at Sydney Cove in 1788.
The Harbour Bridge, opened in 1932, is nicknamed the Coathanger for the shape of its arch.

q.q: Where did James Cook land in 1770, on Sydney's south side?

Q334.t: An island nation ringed by hundreds of waiting ships
Q334.s: Before the city, you notice the sea: hundreds of ships at anchor in the Singapore Strait, scattered like grains of rice. The diamond-shaped island at the tip of the Malay Peninsula has grown by roughly a quarter through land reclamation, and its straight new shorelines are easy to spot. The equator lies less than 150 km to the south.
Q334.w: A diamond-shaped island just off the Malay Peninsula, joined by a causeway, with anchored ships speckling the strait.
f: Stamford Raffles set up a British trading post here in 1819.
The name comes from the Malay Singapura, “lion city”.
Jurong Island, the refining hub in the south-west, was made by joining seven small islands with landfill.

q.q: What does the name “Singapura” mean?

Q8646.t: Green mountains, a crowded shore and a fragrant harbour
Q8646.s: From above, Hong Kong is surprisingly green: steep, forested hills and dozens of islands, with the city packed into thin strips along the shore. Victoria Harbour, a narrow blue channel, separates Kowloon from Hong Kong Island. Further west, look for the airport on a flat man-made platform and a long bridge striking out across the Pearl River estuary.
Q8646.w: Hilly green islands and a peninsula, dense city lining a narrow harbour; a rectangular airport island to the west.
f: About 40 percent of Hong Kong's land is protected as country parks.
The bridge to Zhuhai and Macau is about 55 km long and dips into an undersea tunnel between two artificial islands.
The name means “fragrant harbour”, probably after the incense wood once shipped from here.

q.q: What does the name “Hong Kong” mean?

Q1353.t: Seven cities in one, on the banks of the Yamuna
Q1353.s: Delhi has been rebuilt again and again on the same stretch of the Yamuna, and tradition counts at least seven historic cities layered here. From above, the river runs down the eastern side, braided with sandbars in the dry season. A low, scrubby ridge — the last tip of the ancient Aravalli hills — cuts through the west. At night the glow spreads far across the plain.
Q1353.w: A huge sprawl on a flat plain, a braided river along its east side, a dark wooded ridge through the west.
f: Old Delhi, or Shahjahanabad, was built by Shah Jahan, creator of the Taj Mahal; its Red Fort was finished in 1648.
The Aravalli Range, whose last spur ends in Delhi, is one of the oldest mountain ranges on Earth.
The Iron Pillar near the Qutb Minar has stood for about 1,600 years with remarkably little rust.

q.q: Which river flows past Delhi?

Q269.t: A green oasis city at the foot of the Tian Shan
Q269.s: Tashkent spreads as a broad, leafy grid across an irrigated plain, fed by canals drawn from the Chirchiq River. To the north-east the land rises into the first ridges of the Tian Shan, snowy in winter and spring, and the turquoise Charvak Reservoir fills a mountain valley. Caravans on the Silk Road knew this oasis as Chach.
Q269.w: A large green grid on a flat plain; mountains rising to the north-east with a turquoise reservoir in a valley.
f: The name is usually read as “stone city” in Turkic.
Tashkent's metro, opened in 1977, was the first in Central Asia.
It is the most populous city in Central Asia.

q.q: What does the name “Tashkent” most likely mean?

Q1861.t: City of angels on a looping brown river
Q1861.s: The Chao Phraya winds through Bangkok in lazy brown loops, and the whole city sits on a delta so flat it barely rises above the sea. Around it, rice fields and square fish ponds stretch to the Gulf of Thailand, about 30 km south. Thais rarely say Bangkok: they call it Krung Thep, the city of angels.
Q1861.w: A vast flat grey city on a looping brown river, with a grid of green fields and ponds between it and the gulf.
f: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world.
It became the capital in 1782, when King Rama I moved the court across the river from Thonburi.
Its old network of canals earned Bangkok the nickname “Venice of the East”.

q.q: What do Thais usually call Bangkok?

Q8684.t: A wide river and granite peaks inside one capital
Q8684.s: Seoul is a bowl of city among steep granite mountains, split by the broad Han River. Up to a kilometre wide here, the Han is crossed by more than 25 bridges that show as fine stitches across the water. Joseon kings made it their capital in 1394: mountains behind, a river in front — ideal by the rules of geomancy.
Q8684.w: A broad river curving west through a dense city ringed by rocky, wooded mountains; bridges cross it every kilometre or two.
f: Joseon kings ringed their capital with a stone wall about 18 km long, begun in 1396.
Bukhansan, a national park of granite peaks, rises right on the city's northern edge.
In Korean, the word “Seoul” simply means “capital”.

q.q: Which river flows through Seoul?

Q1461.t: A great round bay, a river and a lake behind the city
Q1461.s: Manila lines the eastern shore of a broad, almost circular bay, famous for its sunsets. The Pasig River threads through the city, linking the bay to Laguna de Bay, the largest lake in the Philippines. For 250 years Spanish galleons sailed from here to Mexico, carrying Chinese silk and porcelain across the Pacific.
Q1461.w: A dense city on the east shore of a wide round bay; a river winds east to a huge lake.
f: The Spanish founded walled Intramuros in 1571; the Manila galleons ran to Acapulco from 1565 to 1815.
The name comes from nilad, a mangrove shrub that once grew along the river.
Laguna de Bay is very shallow: on average it is only about three metres deep.

q.q: Where did the Manila galleons sail to across the Pacific?

Q16959.t: The big city farthest from any sea
Q16959.s: No large city on Earth lies farther from the ocean than Ürümqi — the nearest coastline is about 2,500 km away. It fills a valley on the northern foot of the Tian Shan, with the snowy massif of Bogda Peak rising to the east. North of the city the land flattens into the dry Dzungarian Basin.
Q16959.w: A long city in a valley below snowy mountains; the glaciers of Bogda Peak to the east, dry basin to the north.
f: Bogda Peak is 5,445 m high — and still more than 5 km below you.
The Gurbantünggüt, China's second-largest desert, fills the basin north of the city.
The name comes from Mongolian and means “beautiful pasture”.

q.q: Roughly how far is Ürümqi from the nearest sea?

Q30002.t: A round city on a plain watered since 256 BC
Q30002.s: Chengdu sits on a remarkably flat, green plain on the western edge of the Sichuan Basin, its ring roads drawing concentric circles. Just west, mountains rise abruptly towards the Tibetan Plateau. The plain owes its fertility to Dujiangyan, an irrigation system built around 256 BC that still splits the Min River into a fan of canals.
Q30002.w: A round city of concentric ring roads on a green plain; a wall of mountains rising sharply to the west.
f: An old saying claims Sichuan's dogs bark at the sun because they see it so rarely through the haze.
Dujiangyan, about 50 km north-west of the city, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Chengdu has had a giant panda breeding centre since 1987.

q.q: Which ancient irrigation system still waters the Chengdu Plain?

Q35765.t: Japan's old kitchen, with an airport out in the bay
Q35765.s: Osaka fills the flat land at the head of Osaka Bay, where the Yodo River splits into channels on its way to the sea. The built-up area runs on without a break towards Kobe and Kyoto. Out in the bay, look for a neat rectangle joined to the shore by a single long bridge: Kansai Airport, built on a man-made island.
Q35765.w: A continuous city around the head of a bay; a rectangular airport island offshore, linked by one bridge.
f: Osaka ruled the rice trade in the Edo period so completely that it was called “the nation's kitchen”.
Toyotomi Hideyoshi began building Osaka Castle in 1583.
In neighbouring Sakai, the keyhole-shaped burial mound of Emperor Nintoku is about 486 m long.

q.q: What was Osaka nicknamed in the Edo period?

Q987.t: A planned imperial capital inside a far older city
Q987.s: Within Delhi's endless sprawl, look for a greener, looser patch south of the old city: that is New Delhi. It was planned from scratch after 1911, when Britain decided to move its Indian capital here from Calcutta. Architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker laid out broad avenues meeting at roundabouts, with a ceremonial axis running east from Raisina Hill.
Q987.w: A greener, more open patch in the middle of the Delhi sprawl, a few kilometres west of the Yamuna.
f: New Delhi was formally inaugurated as the capital in 1931, twenty years after the move was announced.
Its plan is built from triangles and hexagons, with avenues radiating out from roundabouts.
The presidential palace on Raisina Hill has about 340 rooms.

q.q: When was New Delhi formally inaugurated as the capital?

Q1355.t: A garden city of lakes on a cool high plateau
Q1355.s: Bengaluru sits about 900 m up on the Deccan Plateau, which keeps it noticeably cooler than India's coastal cities. From above, look for dozens of lakes glinting across the sprawl: most are old reservoirs, or tanks, made centuries ago by damming shallow valleys. A local chieftain, Kempe Gowda, founded the city with a mud fort in 1537.
Q1355.w: A sprawling city on rolling upland, freckled with lakes of all sizes; bare granite hills rise to the north.
f: Its many software companies have earned it the nickname “India's Silicon Valley”.
Lalbagh, a botanical garden begun under Hyder Ali in the 18th century, helped earn it the name “Garden City”.
In 2014 the official name changed from Bangalore to Bengaluru, as it has always been called in Kannada.

q.q: Roughly how high above sea level is Bengaluru?

Q5838.t: A high mountain valley where Babur chose to rest
Q5838.s: Kabul lies about 1,800 m up, in a bowl of bare brown mountains, with rocky ridges rising right through the city itself. The Kabul River winds east from here towards the Khyber Pass and, eventually, the Indus. In winter the snowy wall of the Hindu Kush shines to the north. Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire, loved this valley and chose to be buried here.
Q5838.w: A dense city in a high, dry basin with bare ridges poking through it; snowy mountains to the north.
f: Babur's tomb stands in Bagh-e Babur, a terraced garden he laid out himself.
At about 1,800 m, Kabul stands higher than the summit of Ben Nevis, Britain's highest mountain.
The Kabul River flows east into Pakistan and joins the Indus at Attock.

q.q: Which Mughal emperor chose to be buried in Kabul?

Q3141.t: A city at the head of a vast, nearly closed bay
Q3141.s: Melbourne sits at the top of Port Phillip Bay, a huge sheet of water almost sealed off from the ocean. Its entrance, the Rip, is only about 3 km wide and has a fierce reputation among sailors. The Yarra River curls into the centre from the east, where the forested Dandenong Ranges rise. A gold rush in the 1850s made this one of the richest cities in the world.
Q3141.w: A sprawling city around the head of a huge, almost round bay; wooded hills to the east, flat plains to the west.
f: From 1901 to 1927 Australia's federal parliament sat in Melbourne, until Canberra was ready.
The city was founded in 1835 on the banks of the Yarra.
Port Phillip Bay covers nearly 2,000 km², yet is nowhere deeper than about 24 m.

q.q: Roughly how wide is the entrance to Port Phillip Bay?

Q1867.t: A city poured into a basin of green mountains
Q1867.s: Taipei fills a flat basin like water in a bowl, with forested mountains rising on every side. To the north, the dormant volcanoes of Yangmingshan steam quietly, feeding hot springs on the city's edge. Three rivers join in the basin and leave through a single gap to the north-west as the Tamsui, heading for the Taiwan Strait.
Q1867.w: A dense city filling a round basin, green mountains all around, a river snaking out north-west to the sea.
f: Taipei 101, finished in 2004, was the world's tallest building until 2010.
Qixing Mountain in Yangmingshan, about 1,120 m high, is a dormant volcano within the city limits.
The hot springs of Beitou, on the north side of the city, are heated by the same volcanic group.

q.q: Which river drains the Taipei Basin to the sea?

Q37100.t: A city on a narrow neck between two seas
Q37100.s: Auckland is squeezed onto a narrow isthmus: the Waitematā Harbour opens east to the Pacific, the Manukau Harbour west to the Tasman Sea. The city sits on a field of about 50 small volcanoes, and many survive as green grassy cones among the suburbs. Just offshore, look for Rangitoto, a symmetrical island that rose from the sea only about 600 years ago.
Q37100.w: A city on a thin neck of land between two harbours, dotted with green cones; a round, symmetrical island just offshore.
f: At its narrowest the isthmus is so thin that Māori once hauled canoes across it from one harbour to the other.
Auckland's Māori name, Tāmaki Makaurau, is often translated as “Tāmaki desired by many”.
Rangitoto is both the youngest and the largest volcano in the Auckland field.

q.q: Roughly how many volcanoes make up the Auckland volcanic field?

Q15174.t: A boomtown along Hong Kong's northern edge
Q15174.s: Shenzhen runs in a long ribbon along the coast, facing the green hills of Hong Kong across a narrow river. Before 1980 this was a quiet border district of paddies and fishing villages; that year it became one of China's first Special Economic Zones and began growing at astonishing speed. At night its lights run almost unbroken from the Pearl River estuary to the eastern peninsulas.
Q15174.w: A long band of city along the coast just north of Hong Kong; a bay with a bridge on the west side.
f: The Shenzhen River forms much of the boundary with Hong Kong.
A bridge about 5 km long crosses Shenzhen Bay to Hong Kong's New Territories.
Mangroves still line Shenzhen Bay at Futian, a protected refuge for migrating birds.

q.q: In which year did Shenzhen become a Special Economic Zone?

Q198370.t: A city of scattered towns, and football's ancient home
Q198370.s: Zibo is less one city than a loose cluster of towns, strung out where the hills of central Shandong fall away to the North China Plain. One of them, Linzi, was the capital of the ancient state of Qi and among the largest cities of its age. Another, Boshan, has been known for ceramics and coloured glass for centuries.
Q198370.w: Several separate urban patches spread along the edge of low hills, with the flat plain opening to the north.
f: In 2004 FIFA recognised cuju, played in Linzi over 2,000 years ago, as the earliest known form of football.
Linzi remained the capital of Qi for centuries, until the Qin conquest in 221 BC.

q.q: Zibo's Linzi district is honoured as the birthplace of which sport?

Q1858.t: A thousand-year capital on the rust-brown river
Q1858.s: Hanoi sits on the right bank of the Red River, whose silt-laden water really does look rusty from above. The city is freckled with lakes, the biggest being West Lake in the north. All around, the flat, green Red River Delta is laid out in paddies. The Lý dynasty made this their capital in 1010, calling it Thăng Long, “ascending dragon”.
Q1858.w: A city on the south-west bank of a broad brown river, with a large lake on its north side, amid flat green paddies.
f: The name Hà Nội means roughly “inside the river”; the city received it in 1831.
West Lake, the largest lake in Hanoi, covers about 500 hectares.

q.q: What was Hanoi called when it became the capital in 1010?

Q1854.t: River loops, a vast delta and a maze of mangroves
Q1854.s: The Saigon River loops through the city in tight, shining bends before heading for the sea. South-east of the centre, the land gives way to Cần Giờ, a dark green maze of mangroves and tidal channels. To the south-west spreads the Mekong Delta, one of the great rice bowls of Asia. Many residents still call the city by its old name, Saigon.
Q1854.w: A dense city on a looping river; dark mangrove channels to the south-east, flat green delta to the south-west.
f: The Cần Giờ mangrove forest is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
Before Vietnamese settlers arrived in the 17th century, a Khmer port called Prey Nokor stood here.

q.q: Which mangrove forest lies between Ho Chi Minh City and the sea?

Q11739.t: A Mughal city of gardens on the Punjab plain
Q11739.s: Lahore spreads across the flat Punjab plain, with the Ravi River curving past its north-western edge. Irrigation canals draw straight lines through the fields around it. For centuries this was one of the great cities of the Mughal Empire, and Akbar kept his capital here for more than a decade. The old walled city is still a tight knot of lanes near the river.
Q11739.w: A large flat city with a river on its north-west side and straight canals running through green fields.
f: Akbar held his court at Lahore from 1585 to 1598.
Lahore Fort and the Shalimar Gardens are listed together as one UNESCO World Heritage site.
The walled city was once entered through about a dozen gates.

q.q: Which river flows past Lahore?

Q8660.t: A megacity on a dry coast beside the Indus Delta
Q8660.s: Karachi sprawls over a dry, sand-coloured coast, with bare hills behind it and the Arabian Sea in front. Its harbour is sheltered by a low spit of land, and to the south-east the shore frays into mangrove creeks where the Indus Delta begins. In the 18th century this was a small fishing settlement; today it is Pakistan's largest city.
Q8660.w: A vast beige city on a straight dry coast; a sheltered harbour and mangrove creeks to the south-east, bare hills inland.
f: Its old name was Kolachi, after a fishing village on this shore.
Karachi was Pakistan's capital from 1947 until 1959.
The Indus Delta mangroves to the south-east are among the largest mangrove forests in a dry climate.

q.q: What was Karachi's name as an 18th-century fishing village?

Q18808.t: A river-island city once called the capital of willows
Q18808.s: Pyongyang lies on both banks of the Taedong River, which flows here in wide, calm reaches around long, low islands. Beyond the city, flat farmland and low hills stretch towards the Yellow Sea, about 50 km to the south-west. The name means “flat land”, and in 427 the Goguryeo kingdom moved its capital here.
Q18808.w: A city on both banks of a broad river with long islands; the river winds south-west across flat farmland to the sea.
f: An old name for the city is Ryugyong, “capital of willows”, after the trees along its riverbanks.
Goguryeo ruled from Pyongyang for more than two centuries, from 427 until 668.

q.q: Which river flows through Pyongyang?

Q5972.t: Sumatra's biggest city, built on tobacco
Q5972.s: Medan spreads over the flat coastal plain of north-eastern Sumatra, a few kilometres inland from the Strait of Malacca. Around it, plantations lay out the land in vast, tidy grids. In the 19th century the leaf grown here, Deli tobacco, was prized worldwide as cigar wrapper, and a small village grew rich. To the south-west, volcanic cones rise towards the great caldera lake of Toba.
Q5972.w: A grey sprawl on a flat plain near the coast, ringed by gridded plantations; volcanic peaks on the south-west horizon.
f: Medan is the largest city on Sumatra.
Lake Toba, south of the city, fills the caldera of a supervolcano that erupted about 74,000 years ago.
Deli tobacco, named after the local sultanate, was grown here for cigar wrappers from the 1860s.

q.q: Which crop made Medan rich in the 19th century?

Q1865.t: A muddy river junction that tin turned into a capital
Q1865.s: Kuala Lumpur fills the Klang Valley, with the forested ridges of the Titiwangsa Mountains rising to the east. The city began in the 1850s as a rough camp of tin miners, and many of the lakes glinting around it are old flooded mine pits. To the south, look for Putrajaya, a planned government town wrapped around a large artificial lake.
Q1865.w: A dense city in a green valley, forested mountains to the east, scattered lakes around it and a planned town to the south.
f: Kuala Lumpur means “muddy confluence”: it grew where the Gombak River meets the Klang.
The Petronas Twin Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.
Batu Caves, in a limestone hill on the city's northern edge, have been a Hindu shrine since the 1890s.

q.q: What does the name “Kuala Lumpur” mean?

Q183584.t: A long, thin city squeezed along the Yellow River
Q183584.s: Lanzhou is a city with nowhere to spread: it runs for tens of kilometres along a narrow valley of the Yellow River, hemmed in by bare, ochre loess hills. From above it looks like a grey ribbon laid in a crease of the land. For Silk Road caravans, this was the key crossing of the Yellow River on the way west into the Hexi Corridor.
Q183584.w: A narrow grey ribbon of city following a winding river between bare yellow-brown hills.
f: Zhongshan Bridge, finished in 1909, was the first permanent bridge across the Yellow River.
Before bridges, travellers crossed the river here on rafts buoyed by inflated sheepskins.

q.q: Which river runs through the middle of Lanzhou?

Q179608.t: A green subtropical city in the loops of the Yong
Q179608.s: Nanning coils around the wide meanders of the Yong River, deep in China's subtropical south. The countryside around it is a patchwork of green hills and fields, many of them planted with sugarcane. The border with Vietnam is less than 200 km to the south-west, and since 2004 the city has hosted a yearly trade fair with South-East Asia.
Q179608.w: A city spread around broad river loops, with green hills and fields all around.
f: Guangxi, whose capital is Nanning, grows more than half of China's sugarcane.
Its year-round greenery has earned Nanning the nickname “Green City”.
The Yong River flows on into the Xi River and eventually reaches the Pearl River Delta.

q.q: Which crop makes Guangxi China's biggest producer?

Q192271.t: A high city among countless cone-shaped karst hills
Q192271.s: Guiyang sits about 1,100 m up on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau, and the land around it is crumpled into limestone cones and hollows. Districts squeeze in between the hills, so from above the city looks broken into pieces. An old saying claims Guizhou never has three sunny days in a row or three li of flat ground — look down and you'll see why.
Q192271.w: Patches of city scattered between green, cone-shaped hills on a high, crumpled plateau, often under cloud.
f: Thanks to the altitude, Guiyang's summers are mild for southern China.
The name means “south of Mount Gui”: in Chinese, “yang” marks the sunny side of a hill.

q.q: Guiyang is the capital of which province?

Q11725.t: A mountain city on the point where two rivers meet
Q11725.s: Chongqing's old centre is a steep, crowded peninsula at the meeting of two rivers: the Jialing from the north and the Yangtze. At the tip, their waters often run side by side in two colours before mixing. Around the city, long parallel ridges run north-east like the folds of a rumpled cloth. Hills, fog and hot summers have given it its nicknames: Mountain City and Fog City.
Q11725.w: A dense peninsula between two converging rivers, framed by long parallel ridges running north-east to south-west.
f: The reservoir behind the Three Gorges Dam stretches roughly 600 km upstream, all the way to Chongqing.
Chongqing is counted among China's “furnaces” for its hot, humid summers.
The whole municipality of Chongqing is roughly the size of Austria.

q.q: Which river joins the Yangtze in central Chongqing?

Q68481.t: Banyan City, in a green basin on the Min River
Q68481.s: Fuzhou lies in a basin ringed by green mountains, on the lower Min River just before it widens towards the sea. A large island in the river, Nantai, is itself covered in city. The streets are shaded by banyan trees, first planted here about a thousand years ago, and Fuzhou is still nicknamed Banyan City.
Q68481.w: A city in a mountain-ringed basin on a wide river, with a large built-up island in the middle of the river.
f: The FAO lists Fuzhou's jasmine and tea culture as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System.
Hot springs rise beneath the city centre, and bathhouses have used them for centuries.
The Mawei shipyard, founded in 1866, was one of China's first modern shipyards.

q.q: Fuzhou's nickname comes from which tree?

Q16572.t: Old Canton, at the head of the Pearl River Delta
Q16572.s: Guangzhou sits where the Pearl River breaks into the maze of channels of its delta, and from above it merges seamlessly with the cities around it. The green hump of Baiyun Mountain rises on the northern side. From 1757 to 1842 this was the one Chinese port where Western merchants were allowed to trade, and they knew it as Canton.
Q16572.w: A huge city on a branching river at the top of the delta, with a green mountain on its northern edge.
f: A legend of five rams bringing rice to the people gave Guangzhou its nickname, the City of Rams.
The Canton Fair has been held here twice a year since 1957.

q.q: What did European traders call Guangzhou?

Q59218.t: A patchwork of factory towns on the Pearl River
Q59218.s: Dongguan has no single centre: it is a patchwork of about thirty towns, factory estates and fish ponds on the east side of the Pearl River estuary, filling the gap between Guangzhou and Shenzhen. Countless toys, shoes and electronic gadgets have come out of its workshops. At its western edge, the Humen Bridge leaps across the river mouth.
Q59218.w: A sprawl of towns and ponds on the east shore of a wide estuary, with a long suspension bridge on its western edge.
f: At Humen in 1839, Commissioner Lin Zexu had more than a thousand tonnes of seized opium destroyed.
The Humen Bridge, opened in 1997, has a main span of 888 m.

q.q: What did Commissioner Lin Zexu destroy at Humen in 1839?

Q10389.t: A cool highland basin ringed by volcanoes
Q10389.s: Bandung fills a basin about 700 m up in the highlands of West Java, and the flat floor it sits on was once the bed of a great prehistoric lake. Volcanoes stand all around; the long, flat-topped one to the north is Tangkuban Perahu, the “upturned boat”. Its cool climate and elegant avenues once earned the city the nickname “Paris of Java”.
Q10389.w: A city spread across a flat basin floor, volcanoes on every side; a long, flat-topped mountain to the north.
f: In 1955 Bandung hosted the Asian–African Conference, attended by 29 countries.
Tea plantations cover many of the volcanic slopes around the city.
Legend says Tangkuban Perahu is a boat kicked over in anger by the hero Sangkuriang.

q.q: What does the volcano name Tangkuban Perahu mean?

Q11462.t: A shark, a crocodile and a bridge to Madura
Q11462.s: Surabaya lies on the flat north-east coast of Java, facing the narrow strait that separates it from the island of Madura. Look for the thin line of the Suramadu Bridge, about 5 km long, stitching the two islands together. Along the shore, square fish ponds glint in rows. The city's emblem shows a shark and a crocodile — sura and baya — locked in a fight.
Q11462.w: A large coastal city facing a narrow strait, with a long bridge across to an island and rows of fish ponds along the shore.
f: When the Suramadu Bridge opened in 2009, it was the longest bridge in Indonesia.
Tanjung Perak, Surabaya's harbour, is one of Indonesia's busiest ports.

q.q: Surabaya's emblem shows a shark fighting which animal?

Q5826.t: Where the Silk Road began, below the Qinling wall
Q5826.s: Xi'an lies on the flat Wei River plain, with the Qinling Mountains rising like a dark wall to the south. Its streets still follow a strict north–south grid around a rectangular old core. As Chang'an, this was the capital of the Tang dynasty, the eastern starting point of the Silk Road and one of the largest cities on Earth.
Q5826.w: A big gridded city on a flat plain; a steep mountain wall to the south, a river to the north.
f: Xi'an's Ming-era city wall, about 14 km around, is one of the most complete old city walls in China.
The Terracotta Army was found in 1974 by farmers digging a well, about 35 km to the east.
The Qinling range is China's traditional dividing line between north and south.

q.q: What was Xi'an called as the Tang dynasty capital?

Q72778.t: Coal country's capital along the Fen River
Q72778.s: Taiyuan stretches north to south along the Fen River, in a long basin pinched between two mountain ranges on the Loess Plateau. The hills around it are dry and furrowed, yellow-brown for much of the year. Beneath Shanxi province lies some of China's richest coal, and the city grew as its industrial heart.
Q72778.w: A long city following a river down a narrow basin, bare furrowed hills on both sides.
f: The first fortified town here, Jinyang, was built around 497 BC.
Shanxi is famous for its dark aged vinegar, made around Taiyuan for centuries.

q.q: Which river runs through Taiyuan?

Q11746.t: Three cities split by two rivers and a hundred lakes
Q11746.s: Wuhan is really three old cities — Wuchang, Hankou and Hanyang — divided by the meeting of the Yangtze and its tributary, the Han. From above, the rivers form a giant Y, and lakes glitter everywhere between the districts. The largest, East Lake, spreads its many arms over more than 30 km² on the eastern side.
Q11746.w: Two big rivers meeting in a Y through a vast city, with many lakes; a large branching lake to the east.
f: The first bridge ever built across the Yangtze opened here in 1957.
In the 19th century, Russian merchants ran brick-tea factories in Hankou.
Its place at the heart of China's river network earned Wuhan the nickname “thoroughfare of nine provinces”.

q.q: Which river joins the Yangtze at Wuhan?

Q174091.t: A long orange-grove island in the Xiang River
Q174091.s: Changsha lines both banks of the Xiang River, and in the middle of the river lies a remarkably long, thin island: Orange Isle, once covered in citrus groves. On the west bank rises the wooded hill of Yuelu. At its foot stands one of China's oldest academies, founded in 976 and still part of a university today.
Q174091.w: A city on both banks of a wide river with a long, narrow island in the middle; a wooded hill on the west bank.
f: Orange Isle is about 5 km long, yet very narrow.
The Han-dynasty tombs of Mawangdui, found in Changsha in 1972, held a remarkably well-preserved noblewoman.

q.q: What is the long island in the Xiang River at Changsha called?

Q182852.t: Eternal spring on the shore of a mountain lake
Q182852.s: Kunming sits almost 1,900 m up on the Yunnan plateau, at the northern end of Dian Lake, a long sheet of water whose western shore is lined by steep hills. Altitude and latitude together give it mild weather all year, and it is known as the City of Eternal Spring. The fields around it show the deep red soil typical of the plateau.
Q182852.w: A city at the north end of a long lake with steep hills along its western shore; red-soiled fields around.
f: Dian Lake covers about 300 km², making it the largest lake in Yunnan.
Since the 1980s, black-headed gulls from Siberia have come to Kunming every winter.
The Stone Forest, a UNESCO-listed maze of limestone pinnacles, lies less than 100 km to the south-east.

q.q: What is Kunming's nickname?

Q30340.t: A rail crossroads beside a river that runs above the plain
Q30340.s: Zhengzhou spreads across the flat North China Plain just south of the Yellow River, which here runs wide, braided and sandy between high levees. Its bed has silted up so much that the river flows above the surrounding fields. People have lived here a long time: parts of the rammed-earth walls of a Shang dynasty city, some 3,500 years old, still stand in the centre.
Q30340.w: A big flat grid of a city with a wide, sandy, braided river running east–west just to the north.
f: The Shaolin Temple, cradle of kung fu legend, lies in the Song Mountains less than 100 km to the west.
Zhengzhou grew up where China's main north–south and east–west railways cross.

q.q: Zhengzhou is the capital of which province?

Q11720.t: The Manchu capital before Beijing, on a wintry plain
Q11720.s: Shenyang spreads across the flat plain of north-east China, with the Hun River curving along its southern side; in winter the river freezes and the fields turn white. In 1625 the Manchu leader Nurhaci made it his capital, and his successors ruled from here until they took Beijing in 1644. The Manchus called it Mukden.
Q11720.w: A large flat city on a wide plain, a river along its southern edge; snow-covered and grey in winter.
f: The Mukden Palace, built from 1625, is a smaller cousin of Beijing's Forbidden City and a UNESCO site.
The name means “north of the Shen River”, an old name for the Hun.

q.q: What was Shenyang's Manchu name?

Q170247.t: City of Springs, between Mount Tai and the Yellow River
Q170247.s: Jinan is squeezed between low hills to the south and the Yellow River to the north. Water seeping through the limestone hills bubbles up in the city centre from dozens of springs, which feed Daming Lake and earned Jinan the name City of Springs. On clear days Mount Tai, foremost of China's five sacred mountains, rises about 60 km to the south.
Q170247.w: A city between green hills to the south and a wide river to the north, with a lake in its centre.
f: Tradition counts 72 famous springs in Jinan; the best known is Baotu Spring.
Jinan means “south of the Ji”; since 1855 the Yellow River has flowed in the Ji River's old bed.

q.q: When did the Yellow River shift into its present course past Jinan?

Q11736.t: Beijing's gateway to the sea, edged with salt pans
Q11736.s: Tianjin lies on the flat coastal plain about 120 km south-east of Beijing, where the Hai River winds towards Bohai Bay. Along the shore, look for a geometric pattern of salt evaporation pans and harbour basins in varying shades. The name means “heavenly ford”, given in 1404 by the Yongle Emperor, who had crossed the river here.
Q11736.w: A large city on a flat plain, a winding river to the sea, and a coast of rectangular salt pans and harbour basins.
f: After 1860 several foreign powers held concessions in Tianjin, and their European-style streets survive.
The Changlu salt works along this coast are among the oldest and largest in China.

q.q: What does the name “Tianjin” mean?

Q171943.t: Gateway to a lake that grows and shrinks with the seasons
Q171943.s: Nanchang straddles the Gan River just before it spreads out into the marshy plain of Poyang Lake, China's largest freshwater lake. In summer the lake swells into an inland sea; in winter it can shrink to a web of channels and grassland. Those winter wetlands host the great majority of the world's Siberian cranes.
Q171943.w: A city on both banks of a wide river; to the north-east, the huge, shifting expanse of Poyang Lake.
f: Poyang Lake can cover several thousand km² in the wet season and shrink several times over in the dry.
The Tengwang Pavilion on the Gan River was first built in 653.

q.q: Which lake, China's largest freshwater lake, lies near Nanchang?

Q16666.t: The southern capital, between the Yangtze and green hills
Q16666.s: Nanjing sits on the south bank of the Yangtze, where the river swings north-east on its last stretch to the sea. The forested dome of Purple Mountain rises on the eastern edge, and Xuanwu Lake glints just inside the old walls. The first Ming emperor made this his capital in 1368, and its name still means “southern capital”.
Q16666.w: A large city on the south bank of the broad Yangtze, a green mountain to the east and a lake in its northern part.
f: Nanjing's Ming city wall, about 35 km long, was one of the longest city walls ever built, and much of it survives.
Zhu Yuanzhang, founder of the Ming dynasty, is buried in a tomb on Purple Mountain.

q.q: Which dynasty built Nanjing's great city wall?

Q4970.t: A poets' lake and a river with a racing tidal wave
Q4970.s: Hangzhou wraps around West Lake, a calm sheet of water held on three sides by green hills and praised by Chinese poets for more than a thousand years. South of the city the wide Qiantang River bends towards funnel-shaped Hangzhou Bay. Especially in autumn, a tidal bore charges up the river as a wall of water, drawing crowds to the banks.
Q4970.w: A city on the east shore of a lake with hills on three sides; a wide river curving to a funnel-shaped bay.
f: Hangzhou was the capital of the Southern Song dynasty, and then one of the largest cities in the world.
The Grand Canal, running north to Beijing, begins here.
Longjing, or Dragon Well, one of China's most famous green teas, grows in the hills west of the lake.

q.q: Which river at Hangzhou is famous for its tidal bore?

Q34664.t: A city on the fingers of a delta, by an island sea
Q34664.s: Hiroshima spreads over the delta of the Ōta River, whose channels fan out towards the sea like the fingers of a hand, splitting the city into long islands. Beyond lies the calm Seto Inland Sea, scattered with green islands. The name means “broad island”, and the city was founded in 1589, when the warlord Mōri Terumoto built his castle on the delta.
Q34664.w: A city on a delta of parallel river channels at the head of a bay, with wooded islands scattered offshore.
f: Hiroshima Prefecture produces more than half of Japan's farmed oysters.
Itsukushima Shrine, on the island of Miyajima about 20 km south-west, is famous for its torii gate standing in the sea.

q.q: On the delta of which river is Hiroshima built?

Q92161.t: China's car city on a plain of black earth
Q92161.s: Changchun lies in the middle of the Songliao Plain, a vast, flat expanse of fertile black soil that turns white under snow for months each winter. The city is laid out in a neat grid of wide avenues. In 1953 China's first automobile factory was founded here, and Changchun is still called the cradle of the country's car industry. Its name, ironically for so cold a place, means “long spring”.
Q92161.w: A gridded city on an endless flat plain of dark fields; a forested reservoir on its south-eastern edge.
f: The first trucks built in the People's Republic rolled off the line here in 1956.
Jingyuetan, on the south-eastern edge, is a reservoir ringed by a vast planted forest.

q.q: What is Changchun best known for making?

Q569907.t: Deer City on the Yellow River's great northern bend
Q569907.s: Baotou stretches along the plain between the bare Yin Mountains and the Yellow River, near the top of the river's great loop through Inner Mongolia. Across the water to the south, the dunes of the Kubuqi Desert begin. The city grew into a steel centre in the 1950s, and its Mongolian name is usually translated as “place with deer” — hence its nickname, Deer City.
Q569907.w: An industrial city strung along a plain between bare mountains to the north and a wide river to the south; dunes beyond.
f: Bayan Obo, more than 100 km to the north, is the world's largest known deposit of rare-earth metals.
The Yellow River's loop around the Ordos Plateau is so big that the river flows north, then east, then south.

q.q: Baotou's Mongolian name refers to which animal?

Q42956.t: A railway town on a river that freezes into a festival
Q42956.s: Harbin spreads along the south bank of the Songhua River on the flat plains of the north-east. In winter the river freezes solid into a white road, and blocks cut from its ice are carved into the palaces of the famous Ice and Snow Festival. The city grew from 1898 around a railway built by Russia, and its onion-domed churches still recall those years.
Q42956.w: A large city on the south bank of a wide river with an island park opposite; the river white and frozen in winter.
f: The average January temperature here is well below −15 °C.
Harbin's Ice and Snow Festival has been held every winter since 1985.

q.q: Harbin grew up around a railway built by which country?

Q37951.t: A snowy grid city at the edge of Hokkaido's mountains
Q37951.s: Sapporo was laid out from 1869 on a neat grid, and you can still see its straight lines across the Ishikari Plain, with forested mountains rising right behind it to the west. Few large cities anywhere get as much snow: roughly five metres falls in a typical winter. The name comes from the Ainu language and is often read as “dry, great river”.
Q37951.w: A gridded city on a plain at the foot of forested mountains; in winter, everything white.
f: In 1972 Sapporo hosted the first Winter Olympics held in Asia.
The Sapporo Snow Festival began in 1950 with six snow statues built by local students.

q.q: When did Sapporo host Asia's first Winter Olympics?

Q1361.t: A city of pearls and diamonds among granite boulders
Q1361.s: Hyderabad sits on the rocky Deccan Plateau, where giant granite boulders lie scattered as if dropped by hand. Look for a big lake right in the middle of the city: Hussain Sagar, built in the 16th century, which separates Hyderabad from its twin, Secunderabad. The Qutb Shahi sultans founded the city in 1591, and nearby Golconda was famed for its diamond trade.
Q1361.w: A vast city on a rocky plateau dotted with lakes, a large lake in the centre and a river through the south.
f: The Koh-i-Noor diamond is believed to have come from mines in the Golconda region.
Its centuries-old pearl trade earned Hyderabad the nickname City of Pearls.
The Charminar, the city's four-minareted emblem, was built in 1591, the year Hyderabad was founded.

q.q: Which famous diamond is thought to come from the Golconda mines?

Q1538.t: The Peshwas' city in the lee of the Western Ghats
Q1538.s: Pune sits about 560 m up on the Deccan Plateau, where the Mula and Mutha rivers meet. Just to the west rise the steep, green Western Ghats, with a chain of reservoirs filling their valleys. In the 18th century this was the seat of the Peshwas, chief ministers who ran the Maratha Empire. Today it has so many colleges that it is called the Oxford of the East.
Q1538.w: A large city where two rivers meet on a plateau; green, steep hills and reservoirs to the west.
f: Shaniwar Wada, the Peshwas' fortified palace, was completed in 1732.
The hill fort of Sinhagad stands about 30 km south-west, on a ridge of the Ghats.

q.q: Pune was the seat of which 18th-century rulers?

Q1513.t: Orange City, at the very heart of India
Q1513.s: Nagpur lies close to the geographic centre of India, and a Zero Mile Stone set up by British surveyors still marks the spot. From above it's a sprawling city on a gently rolling plateau, with several lakes on its western side. Orange orchards surround it, giving it the name Orange City, and the forests further out are home to tigers.
Q1513.w: A large city on a flat plateau with a few lakes on its western edge, surrounded by farmland and orchards.
f: Nagpur's oranges are famous across India and carry a geographical indication tag.
Tiger reserves, including Pench and Tadoba, lie within a few hours' drive.

q.q: Nagpur's nickname comes from which fruit?

Q66485.t: The Pink City, laid out on a grid in 1727
Q66485.s: Jaipur spreads across a dry plain in Rajasthan, with the rugged ridges of the Aravalli hills rising to the north and east, where old forts guard the passes. Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II founded it in 1727 on a strict grid, unusual for its time. Its old town is painted terracotta pink, first done to welcome the Prince of Wales in 1876.
Q66485.w: A large city on a dry plain, rocky ridges with forts to the north and east, a lake at their foot.
f: Jai Singh II was also an astronomer; his Jantar Mantar observatory is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The walled city of Jaipur was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2019.

q.q: For whose visit was Jaipur painted pink in 1876?

Q66568.t: An old mill town on the banks of the Ganges
Q66568.s: Kanpur stretches along the south-west bank of the Ganges, which curves past its northern edge in wide, sandy channels. The land all around is the flat, fertile Gangetic plain, laid out in small fields. In the 19th century cotton mills and tanneries turned the town into an industrial hub nicknamed the Manchester of the East. Leather is still one of its big trades.
Q66568.w: A large flat city on the south bank of a broad river with sandbars, surrounded by a patchwork of small fields.
f: Under British rule the city was known as Cawnpore.
Kanpur is one of India's biggest centres of leather tanning.

q.q: Which river flows past Kanpur?

Q80484.t: Ancient Pataliputra, stretched along the wide Ganges
Q80484.s: Patna is long and thin: it runs for many kilometres along the south bank of the Ganges, which here spreads several kilometres wide in flood and breaks into channels around sandbars in the dry season. Look for the long bridge striking north across it. More than 2,000 years ago, as Pataliputra, this was the capital of the Maurya Empire and one of the greatest cities of the ancient world.
Q80484.w: A long, narrow city along the south bank of a very wide, braided river, with a long bridge crossing it.
f: Around 300 BC the Greek envoy Megasthenes described Pataliputra's huge timber walls.
The Mahatma Gandhi Setu, opened in 1982, carries a road about 5.7 km across the Ganges.

q.q: What was Patna called as the Maurya capital?

Q1352.t: Old Madras, facing the Bay of Bengal across a long beach
Q1352.s: Chennai lines a long, straight stretch of the Coromandel Coast, and its signature is Marina Beach: a pale strip of sand running for kilometres beside the Bay of Bengal. Two sluggish rivers, the Cooum and the Adyar, cut through the city to the sea. The English East India Company built Fort St George here in 1644, and the city of Madras grew up around it.
Q1352.w: A flat city along a long, straight sandy coast; harbour breakwaters in the north, two rivers entering the sea.
f: Marina Beach is one of the longest urban beaches in the world.
The city's official name changed from Madras to Chennai in 1996.
Pulicat Lake, a large lagoon about 50 km north, draws flocks of flamingos in winter.

q.q: Which fort did the English build at Chennai in 1644?

Q1070.t: A sultan's city of kites on the Sabarmati
Q1070.s: Ahmedabad spreads across the flat plains of Gujarat on both banks of the Sabarmati, whose course through the city runs straight between long concrete embankments. Sultan Ahmed Shah founded it in 1411, and in 2017 it became the first Indian city on UNESCO's World Heritage list. Each January, at the Uttarayan festival, the sky above it fills with thousands of kites.
Q1070.w: A large flat city split by a river running straight between embankments; a planned capital with green avenues to the north.
f: Gandhi lived at his Sabarmati Ashram on the riverbank from 1917 to 1930.
Gandhinagar, the planned capital of Gujarat, lies about 25 km to the north.

q.q: Which river flows through Ahmedabad?

Q4629.t: Where most of the world's diamonds are cut
Q4629.s: Surat sits on a broad bend of the Tapi River, a few kilometres before it reaches the mudflats of the Arabian Sea coast. In Mughal times it was India's busiest port, and pilgrims sailed from here to Mecca. In the 1610s the English East India Company set up one of its earliest Indian trading posts here. Today the city's workshops cut and polish the great majority of the world's diamonds.
Q4629.w: A dense city on a wide river bend near a flat, muddy coast, with new districts spreading towards the sea.
f: Around nine out of ten of the world's diamonds are cut and polished in Surat.
Surat is also one of India's largest centres of synthetic textiles.

q.q: Surat is famous for cutting and polishing what?

Q1354.t: A river-ringed megacity, once the capital of muslin
Q1354.s: Dhaka is almost an island: the Buriganga, Turag, Balu and Shitalakshya rivers wrap around it, and in the monsoon the fields beyond turn into sheets of water. Inside that ring the city is one of the most densely packed on Earth. In 1610 the Mughals made it the capital of Bengal, and its weavers produced muslin so fine it was likened to woven air.
Q1354.w: A very dense city on slightly higher ground ringed by rivers; in the monsoon, flooded fields all around.
f: Dhaka is often called the rickshaw capital of the world, with hundreds of thousands of cycle rickshaws.
Under the Mughals the city was renamed Jahangirnagar, after Emperor Jahangir.
It has so many mosques that it is nicknamed the City of Mosques.

q.q: Mughal-era Dhaka was famed for which fine fabric?

Q376749.t: Bangladesh's great port, where the hills meet the sea
Q376749.s: Chattogram sits at the mouth of the Karnaphuli River, where the flat delta of Bangladesh finally gives way to green hills rolling east towards Myanmar. It is the country's main seaport. North of the city, look along the shore for a row of large ships deliberately run aground on the mudflats: one of the world's biggest shipbreaking coasts. Portuguese traders called this Porto Grande.
Q376749.w: A port city at a river mouth, green hills to the east; a line of beached ships on the coast to the north.
f: In the yards of Sitakunda, north of the city, ocean-going ships are taken apart on the beach, much of it by hand.
In 2018 the official English spelling changed from Chittagong to Chattogram, closer to the Bengali.

q.q: What did Portuguese traders call Chattogram?

Q3183.t: A lonely capital on a lake-like river of black swans
Q3183.s: Perth is one of the most isolated big cities on Earth: Adelaide, the nearest city of similar size, is over 2,000 km away. The Swan River widens here into broad blue basins that look more like lakes, with the city on their banks. To the east the land rises abruptly at the long, straight line of the Darling Scarp; to the west lie white beaches and Rottnest Island.
Q3183.w: A city around wide, lake-like river basins; a straight escarpment to the east, white beaches and an island to the west.
f: Dutch explorer Willem de Vlamingh named the Swan River in 1697, after its black swans.
Rottnest Island, off the coast, is home to the quokka, a small marsupial with a smiling face.
The Swan River Colony, which grew into Perth, was founded in 1829.

q.q: Who named the Swan River after its black swans in 1697?

Q37995.t: A golden-pagoda city between delta rivers
Q37995.s: Yangon lies on a tongue of land where the Yangon and Bago rivers meet, some 30 km from the Andaman Sea. West of it spreads the vast green Irrawaddy Delta, laced with channels. Two large lakes, Inya and Kandawgyi, glint among the northern districts. Near the second, on a low hill, stands the gilded Shwedagon Pagoda, the most sacred Buddhist site in Myanmar.
Q37995.w: A city on a point of land between converging rivers, with lakes in its northern half; a green delta stretching west.
f: King Alaungpaya named the town Yangon, “end of strife”, in 1755.
Under British rule the city was known as Rangoon.
The Shwedagon's stupa is about 100 m tall and covered in gold plates.

q.q: What does the name “Yangon” mean?

Q572089.t: Karst peaks, a dammed red river and long lives
Q572089.s: Hechi spreads across a rugged corner of north-western Guangxi, where forested limestone peaks crowd so tightly that towns and fields squeeze into the narrow valleys between them. The Hongshui, or Red Water River, winds through deep gorges here and is stepped with big dams. This is a homeland of several minority peoples, among them the Zhuang, Yao, Mulao and Maonan.
Q572089.w: A sea of steep, forested limestone peaks with small towns and fields tucked into the valleys; a dammed river in gorges.
f: Bama county, in Hechi, is famous for its unusually large number of people who live past 100.
Hechi has China's only autonomous counties for the Mulao and the Maonan peoples.
The Longtan Dam on the Hongshui River, in Hechi, feeds one of China's largest hydropower stations.

q.q: Bama county in Hechi is famous for its many…

Q68814.t: Orchards, a delta and round earthen fortresses
Q68814.s: Zhangzhou lies on the fertile plain of the Jiulong, or Nine Dragon River, which widens eastwards into an estuary with Xiamen at its mouth. The land around is a green quilt of orchards, known for lychees, pomelos and narcissus bulbs. In 1567 the Ming lifted their ban on overseas trade at Yuegang, a harbour on this river, and Zhangzhou's goods flowed to Manila and beyond.
Q68814.w: A city on a green delta plain; the river widens east into an estuary towards Xiamen, hills to the west.
f: In the hills west of the city stand Fujian tulou, giant round earthen houses listed by UNESCO.
Zhangzhou's narcissus bulbs are sent all over China for the Lunar New Year.

q.q: What are the giant round earthen houses in Zhangzhou's hills called?

Q205697.t: Kolkata's twin across the Hooghly, with a giant banyan
Q205697.s: Haora, or Howrah, faces Kolkata across the Hooghly River, and from above the two read as one city split by a brown ribbon of water. Bridges stitch them together, and the wide railway yards on this side mark Howrah Station, opened in 1854 and still one of India's busiest. Downstream, the botanic garden at Shibpur shelters the Great Banyan, a single tree grown into a small forest.
Q205697.w: The west-bank half of a city split by a brown river, with bridges across and wide railway yards on this side.
f: The Great Banyan's aerial roots have become thousands of trunks, and its canopy covers well over a hectare.
Howrah Bridge, opened in 1943, was built without nuts and bolts — it is held together by rivets.

q.q: What famous tree grows in the botanic garden at Howrah?

Q38283.t: A fishing village that became Japan's great port
Q38283.s: Yokohama lines the western shore of Tokyo Bay, and from above it flows into Tokyo without a visible border. Its waterfront is a jigsaw of piers, container terminals and reclaimed land, crossed by the long Bay Bridge. In 1859 this was a small fishing village chosen as a port for foreign trade; within decades it had become Japan's gateway to the world.
Q38283.w: A port city on the west side of a large bay, merging into Tokyo; piers, reclaimed land and a bridge over the harbour.
f: Japan's first railway, opened in 1872, ran between Tokyo's Shimbashi and Yokohama.
Yokohama is Japan's second most populous city, after Tokyo.
Its Chinatown is the largest in Japan.

q.q: In which year was Yokohama opened to foreign trade?

Q244898.t: A ring-shaped city wrapped around Taipei
Q244898.s: New Taipei is shaped like a ring: it completely surrounds Taipei, filling the rest of the basin and spilling over green mountains to Taiwan's northern coast. Look for the mouth of the Tamsui River, where an old harbour town faces the sunset, and the rocky capes of the far north. With nearly four million people, it is the most populous city in Taiwan.
Q244898.w: A band of city and green hills encircling Taipei, reaching the sea at a river mouth and at rocky northern capes.
f: The Spanish built the first Fort San Domingo at Tamsui in 1628.
Fuguijiao, the northernmost point of Taiwan's main island, lies within the city.
Yehliu, on its north coast, is famous for mushroom-shaped rocks carved by the sea.

q.q: Who built the first Fort San Domingo at Tamsui in 1628?

Q16520.t: A port city wedged between steep hills and the sea
Q16520.s: Busan is squeezed into the gaps between steep green ridges and a ragged, bay-cut coastline at Korea's south-eastern tip. To the west, the Nakdong River ends in a delta of sandbars and reed beds that shelters migrating birds. Long bridges leap across the bays. On a clear day, Japan's island of Tsushima is visible about 50 km offshore.
Q16520.w: A long city threaded between steep ridges along an indented coast; a river delta with sandbars to the west.
f: Busan is South Korea's largest port and one of the busiest container ports in the world.
In the Joseon era, Busan hosted a walled Japanese trading post known as the Waegwan.

q.q: Which Japanese island can be seen from Busan on clear days?

Q74881.t: A peninsula-tip port between two seas
Q74881.s: Dalian occupies the hilly southern tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, where the Bohai Sea meets the Yellow Sea. Its coast is cut into bays, headlands and harbours. Russia founded the modern city in 1898 under the name Dalny, meaning “distant”, and laid it out with round plazas and streets radiating from them like spokes.
Q74881.w: A hilly peninsula tip with a jagged coast of bays and harbours; open sea on both sides.
f: Dalian's harbour stays largely free of ice in winter, a rarity in northern China.
Lüshun, once known as Port Arthur, sits at the very tip of the peninsula.

q.q: Under what name did Russia found Dalian in 1898?

Q11751.t: Castle city on a plain of three parallel rivers
Q11751.s: Nagoya spreads over the flat Nōbi Plain at the head of Ise Bay. Just to the west, three big rivers — the Kiso, Nagara and Ibi — run side by side to the sea like parallel strokes of a brush. Offshore to the south, the airport sits on its own man-made island. Tokugawa Ieyasu had Nagoya Castle built in the 1610s, and the city grew up around it.
Q11751.w: A large city on a flat plain at the head of a bay; three parallel rivers to the west, an airport island to the south.
f: Atsuta Shrine in Nagoya is said to house the Kusanagi sword, one of Japan's three imperial regalia.
Toyota's home city lies just east of Nagoya, making the region the heart of Japan's car industry.

q.q: Which legendary sword is said to be kept at Atsuta Shrine?

Q28729.t: Where Vasco da Gama reached India, under coconut palms
Q28729.s: Kozhikode sits on the Malabar Coast, a city half-hidden under a thick green blanket of coconut palms between the Arabian Sea and the rising Western Ghats. As Calicut, it was the busy capital of the Zamorin kings and a hub of the pepper trade. In 1498 Vasco da Gama landed nearby, completing the first sea voyage from Europe to India.
Q28729.w: A city under a dense green canopy of palms along a straight coast, with mountains rising to the east.
f: Calico, a plain cotton cloth, takes its name from Calicut.
Zheng He's Chinese treasure fleets called at Calicut in the early 15th century.

q.q: Which cloth takes its name from Calicut?

Q171771.t: Temple City at the edge of the Mahanadi delta
Q171771.s: Bhubaneswar sits on slightly raised red-earth land at the south-western edge of the Mahanadi delta, where green paddies stretch towards the Bay of Bengal. Hundreds of stone temples once stood here, and it is still called the Temple City. The modern town was planned from 1948 as the new capital of Odisha, right beside the ancient one.
Q171771.w: A city on low reddish uplands, with the green, river-laced delta spreading east and north towards the coast.
f: The Lingaraja Temple, the city's greatest, dates largely from the 11th century.
The rock-cut caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri, on the western edge, were carved for Jain monks over 2,000 years ago.
Chilika, India's largest coastal lagoon, lies about 100 km to the south-west.

q.q: What is Bhubaneswar's nickname?

Q200054.t: India's steel city, planned around a single works
Q200054.s: Jamshedpur grew around a steel plant founded in 1907 on the Chota Nagpur Plateau, where iron ore, coal and water lay close together. From above, look for the dark block of the steelworks near the meeting of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers, with green planned neighbourhoods around it. The forested Dalma Hills to the north shelter wild elephants.
Q200054.w: A planned town where two rivers meet, a large dark industrial block at its centre, forested hills to the north.
f: The city is named after Jamsetji Tata, who dreamed up the steelworks but died before it was built.
It was one of India's first planned industrial cities.

q.q: Jamshedpur is named after which industrialist?

Q5753.t: Timur's blue-domed capital in a green Silk Road oasis
Q5753.s: Samarkand is a green oasis in the valley of the Zarafshan, whose name means “gold-scattering”, with brown mountain ridges rising to the south. On the city's northern edge lies Afrasiyab, a bare, empty mound that was the city for its first two thousand years. Timur made Samarkand his capital in 1370 and filled it with turquoise domes.
Q5753.w: A green oasis in a wide river valley, brown ridges to the south, a bare earthen mound on the northern edge.
f: Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg built a great observatory here in the 1420s.
At around 2,700 years old, Samarkand is one of the oldest cities in Central Asia.
From the 8th century, Samarkand paper was prized across the Islamic world.

q.q: Which ruler made Samarkand his capital in 1370?

Q9310.t: A small capital between steep mountains and a reef island
Q9310.s: Dili is a low, compact city on a narrow strip of flat land along Timor's north coast, with steep mountains rising close behind it. Across the strait, about 25 km to the north, lies Atauro Island, fringed with coral reefs. The Portuguese moved their colonial capital here in 1769, and Portuguese is still one of the country's official languages.
Q9310.w: A small city on a thin coastal plain, steep mountains behind, a long island across the water to the north.
f: Surveys around Atauro have recorded some of the highest reef-fish diversity anywhere.
Timor lies in Wallacea, the transition zone between Asian and Australian wildlife.

q.q: When did the Portuguese move their Timor capital to Dili?

Q37806.t: A small harbour capital among reefs and lagoons
Q37806.s: Port Vila curls around a sheltered harbour on the south-west coast of Efate, one of about 80 islands of Vanuatu. From above, look for the turquoise of reefs and lagoons against dark green hills, and the small islets in the bay. Until 1980 these islands were the New Hebrides, ruled jointly by Britain and France — an unusual arrangement known as a condominium.
Q37806.w: A small town around a sheltered bay, turquoise reefs and lagoons along the shore, green hills behind.
f: Vanuatu's national language, Bislama, is a creole largely based on English.
Land diving on Pentecost Island, to the north, is often described as the forerunner of bungee jumping.

q.q: What were Vanuatu's islands called before 1980?

Q9365.t: A city named after a Monday market, below snowy peaks
Q9365.s: Dushanbe fills a broad green valley where the Varzob River tumbles out of the Hissar Range, whose snowy ridges rise just north of the city. A century ago this was a village known for its weekly bazaar, held on Mondays — and “dushanbe” is simply Tajik for Monday. East of here, the Vakhsh River is held back by some of the tallest dams on Earth.
Q9365.w: A green city in a wide valley at the foot of snowy mountains to the north, with a river flowing down through it.
f: The Nurek Dam on the Vakhsh, about 75 km east, is around 300 m high.
From 1929 to 1961 the city was called Stalinabad.

q.q: What does “Dushanbe” mean in Tajik?

Q1362.t: A planned grid capital at the foot of the Margalla Hills
Q1362.s: Islamabad is one of the world's newer capitals, laid out from the 1960s on a neat grid of sectors, each with its own green belt. From above it looks tidy and leafy, pressed against the forested Margalla Hills — the first foothills of the Himalaya. Just south, its older twin Rawalpindi forms a much denser, busier sprawl.
Q1362.w: A neat grid of green sectors along the foot of wooded hills, with a lake to the east and a denser city to the south.
f: Greek planner Constantinos Doxiadis drew up Islamabad's master plan.
Its sectors are named with a letter and a number, like squares on a chessboard.
Rawal Lake, on the eastern edge, is a reservoir that supplies water to both cities.

q.q: Who drew up Islamabad's master plan?

Q185453.t: An ancient City of Saints on the hot Punjab plain
Q185453.s: Multan lies on the flat, irrigated plain of southern Punjab, with the braided Chenab River a few kilometres to the west. It is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in South Asia, and its many Sufi shrines have earned it the name City of Saints. An old Persian couplet lists Multan's four gifts: dust, heat, beggars and graveyards.
Q185453.w: A large city on a flat plain of fields and canals, a wide braided river to the west, orchards around.
f: The tomb of the Sufi saint Shah Rukn-e-Alam, built in the 14th century, is an octagonal brick landmark.
Multan is famous across Pakistan for its mangoes.
Blue-glazed tiles and pottery are a centuries-old local craft.

q.q: Multan is traditionally known as the City of…

Q1640079.t: A city of windcatchers on the banks of the Indus
Q1640079.s: Hyderabad sits on a low limestone ridge on the east bank of the Indus, about 150 km upriver from Karachi. The river here is wide and braided, and a barrage beside the city spreads its water into canals that turn the desert green. The Kalhora ruler Ghulam Shah founded the city in 1768. Its old houses once bristled with rooftop windcatchers that funnelled breezes indoors.
Q1640079.w: A city on a low ridge beside a wide, braided river, with a barrage across it and green canal-fed fields around.
f: Hyderabad is known as the city of bangles for its many glass-bangle workshops.
The Kotri Barrage beside the city diverts Indus water into irrigation canals.

q.q: What did old houses in Hyderabad, Sindh, carry on their roofs?

Q1113311.t: A frontier city at the foot of the Khyber Pass
Q1113311.s: Peshawar sits in a green, fertile basin ringed by bare brown mountains, just east of where the Khyber Pass climbs west towards Afghanistan. The Kabul River loops across the valley to the north. As Purushapura, it was the capital of the Kushan king Kanishka nearly two thousand years ago, and for centuries caravans rested here before or after the pass.
Q1113311.w: A dense city on a green plain encircled by bare mountains, with a gap leading west into the hills.
f: Kanishka raised a huge Buddhist stupa here, described by Chinese pilgrims as one of the tallest structures of its day.
The name of the old Qissa Khwani Bazaar means “storytellers' market”.

q.q: What was Peshawar called as the Kushan capital?

Q3037.t: A valley that was once a lake, beneath the Himalaya
Q3037.s: Kathmandu fills an almost round valley about 1,400 m up, ringed by terraced green hills. Geologists confirm what legend says: the valley floor was once a lake, and its drained sediments made the soil here so fertile. On a clear day, a wall of snowy Himalayan peaks shines along the northern horizon.
Q3037.w: A round, densely built valley ringed by terraced hills; on clear days, a wall of snow peaks to the north.
f: The valley holds seven groups of monuments on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
The city's name is traced to Kasthamandap, a wooden pavilion said to have been built from a single tree.
Everest, about 160 km to the east, is only some 2 km below your cruising altitude.

q.q: Legend and geology agree the Kathmandu Valley was once…

Q36526.t: A tropical capital on a surprisingly dry, brown coast
Q36526.s: Port Moresby wraps around a harbour on the south coast of New Guinea, and it looks surprisingly dry for the tropics: its hills turn brown and grassy in the dry season because they lie in a rain shadow. Coral reefs fringe the coast. Inland, the forested Owen Stanley Range rises to peaks of about 4,000 m. Captain John Moresby named the harbour in 1873 after his father.
Q36526.w: A town spread around a harbour and bays, brown grassy hills behind, reefs offshore and high mountains inland.
f: Hanuabada, a village of houses on stilts over the harbour, is the traditional home of the Motu people.
Motu traders once sailed big lakatoi canoes along the coast on trading voyages called hiri.

q.q: Captain John Moresby named the harbour in 1873 after…

Q40921.t: A strip of town below Guadalcanal's green mountains
Q40921.s: Honiara is a thin strip of town along the north coast of Guadalcanal, squeezed between the sea and grassy foothills that climb towards jungle-covered mountains. The island's highest peaks, over 2,300 m, are the tallest in the Solomon Islands. Spanish navigator Álvaro de Mendaña reached these islands in 1568 and named them after King Solomon, hoping for gold.
Q40921.w: A narrow town along a coast, green hills and high mountains behind it, islands across the water to the north.
f: The name Honiara is often said to come from a local phrase meaning “facing the south-east wind”.
Guadalcanal is named after a town in Andalusia, Spain, home of one of Mendaña's officers.

q.q: Who named the Solomon Islands in 1568?

Q976.t: Siberia's old university town, lace-carved in wood
Q976.s: Tomsk sits on the high right bank of the Tom River, surrounded by dark taiga that stretches to every horizon. Cossacks founded a fort here in 1604 on the orders of Tsar Boris Godunov. In 1888 the city opened the first university in Siberia, and it is still a student town. Many old wooden houses are decorated with carvings as delicate as lace.
Q976.w: A city on the high east bank of a winding river, surrounded by dark coniferous forest; white in winter.
f: Tomsk State University, opened in 1888, was the first university in Asian Russia.
The city keeps hundreds of historic wooden houses with carved window frames.

q.q: When did Tomsk open Siberia's first university?

Q7978.t: Russia's easternmost town, at the mouth of a tundra river
Q7978.s: Anadyr is a small town on a point of land at the mouth of the Anadyr River, where it opens into a wide estuary of the Bering Sea. Around it lies treeless tundra on permafrost, white for much of the year. It is the easternmost town in Russia, just two and a half degrees west of the 180th meridian, and about 10,000 people live here.
Q7978.w: A small cluster of town on a point of land at a wide estuary, surrounded by flat, treeless tundra.
f: The town was founded in 1889 under the name Novo-Mariinsk.
The estuary is frozen for much of the year, from autumn well into early summer.

q.q: What was Anadyr called when it was founded in 1889?

Q887.t: An ironworks town in the Urals, on the edge of Asia
Q887.s: Yekaterinburg spreads across the low, forested hills of the Middle Urals, just east of the watershed traditionally taken as the border between Europe and Asia. It began in 1723 as an ironworks, and the dam built to power it still holds back the City Pond in the centre. The city is named after Catherine I, wife of Peter the Great.
Q887.w: A big city among low forested hills, a dammed pond on the river in its centre and many lakes around.
f: Monuments marking the Europe–Asia border stand on the ridge less than 20 km west of the city.
From 1924 to 1991 the city was called Sverdlovsk.

q.q: Yekaterinburg is named after which empress?

Q183002.t: An oil town among bogs and lakes on the great Ob
Q183002.s: Surgut stands on the right bank of the Ob, in the middle of the West Siberian Plain — one of the flattest, boggiest places on Earth, speckled with countless lakes. Around it lie some of Russia's largest oilfields; look for straight roads linking square well pads across the swamp. At night, isolated gas flares glow in the darkness.
Q183002.w: A city on a broad river amid endless bogs and lakes, crossed by straight roads; flares glowing at night.
f: Founded in 1594, Surgut is one of the oldest Russian towns in Siberia.
Its bridge over the Ob, opened in 2000, hangs from a single tall pylon.

q.q: In which year was Surgut founded?

Q6014.t: A silver town where ribbons of pine cross the steppe
Q6014.s: Barnaul stands on the high left bank of the Ob, where fields and steppe begin to replace the taiga. Look for a strange pattern south-west of the city: long, narrow strips of dark pine forest running straight across the farmland, like ribbons laid on a table. The town grew from 18th-century smelting works, and for decades it produced most of Russia's silver.
Q6014.w: A city on the high bank of a wide river; long, straight dark strips of pine forest running diagonally across the fields.
f: The ribbon pine forests follow ancient channels carved by meltwater, and some stretch for hundreds of kilometres.
The first smelting works here was set up in the 1730s by the industrialist Akinfiy Demidov.

q.q: Which river does Barnaul stand on?

Q883.t: Siberia's biggest city, born where a railway crossed the Ob
Q883.s: Novosibirsk straddles the Ob, and its reason to exist is a bridge: in 1893 the Trans-Siberian Railway crossed the river here, and a settlement sprang up beside the works. In barely a century it became the largest city in Siberia. South of the city, a dam has turned the Ob into a reservoir some 200 km long that locals call the Ob Sea.
Q883.w: A big city on both banks of a wide river crossed by several bridges; a vast, long reservoir stretches south.
f: The city was called Novonikolayevsk until 1926.
Akademgorodok, a science town founded in the 1950s, lies in the pine forest beside the Ob Sea.

q.q: What was Novosibirsk called when it was founded?

Q35381.t: A harbour city with brand-new land built into the sea
Q35381.s: Colombo lines the flat west coast of Sri Lanka, its harbour sheltered behind long breakwaters. Right beside it, look for a large, geometric block of new land pushed out into the Indian Ocean — a whole district built on reclaimed sand. Portuguese, Dutch and British traders each held the port in turn. Inland, green hills rise towards the mountains at the island's heart.
Q35381.w: A flat coastal city, a harbour behind breakwaters and a geometric block of reclaimed land jutting into the sea.
f: Sri Lanka's official capital, Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, borders Colombo on its eastern side.
Colombo's harbour is man-made: work on its first great breakwater began in 1875.

q.q: Which city is Sri Lanka's official capital, next to Colombo?

Q1467.t: Where Spain's story in the Philippines began
Q1467.s: Cebu City lies on the east coast of a long, narrow, mountainous island, facing flat Mactan Island across a slim channel crossed by bridges; the airport sits on Mactan. Magellan's expedition arrived here in 1521 and planted a cross that is still venerated. In 1565 Miguel López de Legazpi founded the first Spanish settlement in the archipelago on this shore.
