Q1467.w: A city on the east coast of a long, hilly island, facing a flat island with an airport across a narrow channel.
f: On Mactan in 1521, Magellan fell in a clash with the chief Lapu-Lapu, now honoured as a national hero.
Cebu is regarded as the oldest city in the Philippines.

q.q: In which year did Magellan's expedition plant a cross at Cebu?

Q459787.t: An old sugar port facing a mango island
Q459787.s: Iloilo spreads over flat land on the south coast of Panay, facing the hilly island of Guimaras across a strait only a few kilometres wide. Rivers and fish ponds break up the city's edges. When the port opened to world trade in 1855, sugar from nearby Negros poured through it, and grand merchant houses rose along its streets.
Q459787.w: A flat city on a coast facing a hilly island across a narrow strait, with rivers and fish ponds around.
f: Guimaras, across the strait, is famous for its sweet mangoes.
Miag-ao Church, about 40 km to the west, is a UNESCO-listed Baroque church of yellow stone from the 18th century.

q.q: Iloilo faces which island across a narrow strait?

Q1473.t: A gulf city beneath the highest peak in the Philippines
Q1473.s: Davao spreads along the shore of the Davao Gulf in south-eastern Mindanao, with the green island of Samal just across the water. To the west rises Mount Apo, a volcanic peak of 2,954 m and the highest mountain in the Philippines. The land in between is carpeted with banana and fruit plantations, and Davao is famous for its durian.
Q1473.w: A long city on the shore of a wide gulf with an island just offshore; a large volcanic mountain to the west.
f: Davao is the largest city in the Philippines by land area.
The rare Philippine eagle nests in the forests around Mount Apo.

q.q: Which is the highest mountain in the Philippines?

Q132732.t: A town beside one of the world's largest man-made lakes
Q132732.s: Bratsk sits beside an enormous reservoir that fills the valleys of the Angara and its tributaries, reaching through the taiga in long, branching arms. The dam, finished in the 1960s, powered one of the largest hydroelectric stations of its time. The town itself is scattered in separate districts along the shores. A Cossack fort stood here as early as 1631.
Q132732.w: A huge, many-armed reservoir winding through dark taiga, with a dam and scattered districts of town along its shores.
f: The Bratsk Reservoir holds about 170 km³ of water, one of the largest reservoirs in the world by volume.
When it was completed, the Bratsk hydroelectric station was the most powerful in the world.

q.q: A dam on which river created the Bratsk Reservoir?

Q6576.t: The gateway to Baikal, on the lake's only outflow
Q6576.s: Irkutsk lies on both banks of the Angara, the only river that flows out of Lake Baikal, some 60 km upstream. A dam just above the city has widened the river into a long reservoir. On a clear day, look south-east for Baikal itself: a deep-blue crescent framed by mountains, the deepest lake on Earth. Irkutsk began as a fort in 1661 and grew rich on tea and furs.
Q6576.w: A city on both banks of a wide river with a reservoir upstream; the long, deep-blue arc of Lake Baikal to the south-east.
f: Lake Baikal is over 1,600 m deep and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.
Many Decembrists exiled after 1825 settled in Irkutsk and shaped its cultural life.

q.q: How many rivers flow out of Lake Baikal?

Q919.t: A Yenisei city where the river never freezes
Q919.s: Krasnoyarsk lines both banks of the mighty Yenisei, with forested hills and rocky outcrops rising to the south. Upstream, a huge dam releases water that is warmer than the winter air, so the river through the city stays open and steams even at −30 °C. The city began in 1628 as a Cossack fort named after a red clay cliff on the riverbank.
Q919.w: A large city on both banks of a very wide river, forested hills and rock pillars to the south; in winter, open water steaming.
f: Stolby, a reserve of giant granite pillars in the taiga, begins right on the city's southern edge.
The Krasnoyarsk Dam, about 30 km upstream, is one of the most powerful hydroelectric stations in Russia.
The city's Communal Bridge appears on the Russian 10-rouble banknote.

q.q: What does the name Krasnoyarsk refer to?

Q678299.t: An Arctic outpost where the Yenisei meets the Kara Sea
Q678299.s: Dikson is a tiny settlement on bare, rocky shores where the vast gulf of the Yenisei opens into the Kara Sea. For much of the year both sea and land are white, and the town is little more than a scatter of buildings on the tundra. Only about a thousand people live here, far above the Arctic Circle, where the sun does not rise for weeks in midwinter.
Q678299.w: A tiny scatter of buildings on a rocky Arctic shore at the mouth of a huge, ice-covered gulf.
f: Nordenskiöld named the harbour in 1875 after Oscar Dickson, the Swedish merchant who funded his expeditions.
The polar night here lasts about two and a half months.
Its port has served ships on the Northern Sea Route.

q.q: Oscar Dickson, after whom Dikson is named, came from which country?

Q53139.t: A sunny Transbaikal city between low forested ridges
Q53139.s: Chita lies in a broad valley where the Chita River meets the Ingoda, framed by low ridges of larch and pine. Transbaikalia is one of Russia's sunniest regions, and in winter the ground often stays bare under a hard, dry frost. From 1827 many exiled Decembrists were held here, and the wives who followed them helped turn a small fort into a town.
Q53139.w: A city in a wide valley between low wooded ridges, where two rivers meet; a large lake on its western edge.
f: The Trans-Siberian Railway passes through Chita on its way to the Pacific.
The sun shines here for well over 2,000 hours a year.

q.q: Which famous exiles were held in Chita from 1827?

Q959.t: The Trans-Siberian's end, on a hilly peninsula of bays
Q959.s: Vladivostok climbs over the hills of a peninsula between two bays of the Sea of Japan, and its harbour, the Golden Horn, was named after Istanbul's. Look south for the long, fine line of a bridge to Russky Island. The city was founded in 1860, and it is the eastern end of the Trans-Siberian Railway, about 9,300 km from Moscow.
Q959.w: A hilly city on a peninsula between two bays, a curved harbour in the middle and a long bridge south to an island.
f: The Russky Bridge, opened in 2012, had the longest cable-stayed span in the world: 1,104 m.
The name joins the Russian words for “rule” and “east”.

q.q: Vladivostok's harbour is named after which bay in Istanbul?

Q1993488.t: A remote river port near the delta of the Yana
Q1993488.s: Nizhneyansk — “Lower Yana” — is a tiny settlement on the tundra near where the Yana River splits into a delta and meets the Laptev Sea. From above, the land around is freckled with countless thaw lakes, frozen and white for most of the year. Only a few hundred people remain in what was once a busier river port on this remote Arctic coast.
Q1993488.w: A tiny settlement on flat tundra dotted with lakes, near a river breaking into many channels towards the sea.
f: Far upstream on the Yana lies Verkhoyansk, one of the coldest inhabited places in the Northern Hemisphere.
On the lower Yana, archaeologists have found traces of people living in the Arctic about 32,000 years ago.

q.q: Which famously cold town lies upstream on the Yana?

Q6610.t: The coldest big city, on a river kilometres wide
Q6610.s: Yakutsk sits on the west bank of the Lena, which here spreads into a maze of channels and islands several kilometres wide. It is often called the coldest major city on Earth: January averages near −40 °C, and ice fog can hang over the streets for days. The whole city stands on permafrost, so most buildings rest on piles driven deep into the frozen ground.
Q6610.w: A city on the west bank of an extremely wide, island-studded river, flat taiga all around; ice fog in winter.
f: Cossacks led by Pyotr Beketov founded a fort on the Lena here in 1632.
The Lena Pillars, a UNESCO-listed wall of rock towers, stand beside the river about 200 km upstream.

q.q: Why do most buildings in Yakutsk stand on piles?

Q500895.t: A polar port beside the vast fan of the Lena Delta
Q500895.s: Tiksi is a small Arctic port on a bay of the Laptev Sea, backed by bare, low mountains. Just to the west spreads one of the great sights of the north: the Lena Delta, a fan of hundreds of channels and thousands of lakes, around 30,000 km² in all. For most of the year the sea here is frozen, and in midwinter the sun stays below the horizon for weeks.
Q500895.w: A small port on an icy bay; to the west, a gigantic delta fanning out into countless channels and lakes.
f: The Lena Delta is the largest delta in the Arctic and a protected nature reserve.
Tiksi has served ships on the Northern Sea Route since the 1930s.

q.q: Which river's vast delta lies just west of Tiksi?

Q7968.t: A port between two bays of the Sea of Okhotsk
Q7968.s: Magadan sits on a neck of land between two bays of the Sea of Okhotsk, Nagaev and Gertner, with bare, rounded mountains rising behind it. In winter the sea freezes and the coast turns a uniform white. For most travellers this is where the Kolyma region begins: a vast land of mountains, gold-bearing rivers and larch forest stretching inland.
Q7968.w: A city on a narrow neck of land between two bays, bare hills behind; sea ice along the coast in winter.
f: The Kolyma Highway links Magadan with Yakutsk, about 2,000 km away.
The Kolyma basin inland has been one of Russia's main gold-mining regions since the 1930s.

q.q: Which sea does Magadan stand on?

Q230628.t: A mining city beside a giant open-pit crater
Q230628.s: Erdenet lies among rolling green hills in northern Mongolia, and next to it you can't miss the mine: a vast, terraced grey pit and a broad, pale tailings pond. The town was built from 1974 to serve one of the largest copper deposits in Asia. Its name means roughly “with treasure”.
Q230628.w: A small city in green steppe hills, beside a huge terraced grey pit and a large pale tailings pond.
f: Besides copper, the Erdenet mine produces molybdenum, a metal used to harden steel.
Copper concentrate is one of Mongolia's main exports.

q.q: What is mainly mined at Erdenet?

Q23430.t: The world's coldest capital, in a steppe valley
Q23430.s: Ulaanbaatar stretches east–west along the valley of the Tuul River, with the forested ridge of Bogd Khan Mountain rising to the south and pale ger districts spilling up the hills to the north. Around it the treeless steppe rolls to the horizon. With an average yearly temperature below freezing, it is the coldest national capital on Earth.
Q23430.w: A long city in a wide river valley, a dark forested mountain to the south, bare rolling steppe all around.
f: The city began in 1639 as a moving monastery camp and only settled on this spot in 1778.
Bogd Khan Mountain has been protected since the 18th century, making it one of the oldest nature reserves in the world.
The name means “red hero”; the city took it in 1924.

q.q: Among the world's capitals, Ulaanbaatar is the…

Q695360.t: A tiny Koryak capital near the Okhotsk shore
Q695360.s: Palana is a small settlement in the valley of the Palana River, a few kilometres from the Sea of Okhotsk on Kamchatka's remote north-west coast. Around it lies a wild country of tundra, dwarf pine and snow-streaked ridges rising towards the Sredinny Range. It is the administrative centre of the Koryak district, homeland of the Koryak people, reindeer herders and sea hunters.
Q695360.w: A small settlement in a river valley near the sea, amid tundra and low mountains; snow lingers on the ridges into summer.
f: Palana was the capital of the Koryak Autonomous Okrug until it merged into Kamchatka Krai in 2007.
The settlement is so remote that most visitors arrive by plane.

q.q: Palana lies in the homeland of which people?

Q7951.t: A harbour city at the foot of two smoking volcanoes
Q7951.s: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky lines the shore of Avacha Bay, one of the finest natural harbours in the world, and behind it rise two giant cones: Koryaksky, about 3,456 m, and the often steaming Avachinsky. No road links the city to the rest of Russia; everything comes by sea or air. Vitus Bering founded it in 1740 and named it after his two ships.
Q7951.w: A city along a wide, nearly enclosed bay, with two big snow-streaked volcanic cones right behind it.
f: Bering's ships were the St Peter and the St Paul — hence the city's name.
Kamchatka has around 30 active volcanoes, and several can be seen from the city on a clear day.

q.q: Bering named the city after his two ships: the St Peter and the…

Q7253.t: Home of rendang, between the ocean and the volcanoes
Q7253.s: Padang lies on a narrow coastal plain in West Sumatra, pressed between the Indian Ocean and the steep green wall of the Barisan Mountains, with volcanoes rising inland. It is the main city of the Minangkabau people, known for houses whose roofs curve up like buffalo horns. Their cooking, from rendang to fiery curries, is served in “Padang restaurants” all over Indonesia.
Q7253.w: A city on a thin coastal plain, steep green mountains behind, the open ocean in front and islands offshore.
f: The Minangkabau are among the largest matrilineal societies in the world: land passes down through the women.
Legend says the name Minangkabau means “victorious buffalo”.

q.q: Among the Minangkabau, family land passes down through…

Q9361.t: A leafy grid city beneath a wall of snowy peaks
Q9361.s: Bishkek lies on the flat floor of the Chuy Valley, laid out on a green grid of tree-lined streets. Immediately to the south the Kyrgyz Ala-Too range rises like a wall, its peaks above 4,000 m snowy for most of the year. The city grew from Pishpek, a clay fortress built by the Khanate of Kokand in 1825.
Q9361.w: A green, gridded city on a flat valley floor, with a steep wall of snowy mountains just to the south.
f: From 1926 to 1991 the city was called Frunze.
Ala Archa National Park, a gorge of glaciers and juniper, begins only about 40 km south of the centre.
The Chuy River, north of the city, forms part of the border with Kazakhstan.

q.q: What was Bishkek called from 1926 to 1991?

Q532560.t: Where the Ming Great Wall ends, in the Gobi
Q532560.s: Jiayuguan stands at the narrowest point of the Hexi Corridor, a gap between the snowy Qilian Mountains to the south and bare desert hills to the north. This is where the Ming dynasty ended its Great Wall: the fortress of Jiayu Pass, first built in 1372, guarded the road west. Around the modern steel town, green oasis fields fade quickly into stony gobi.
Q532560.w: A small city in a narrow corridor of desert, snow-capped mountains to the south, stony plains all around.
f: Jiayu Pass was nicknamed the “First and Greatest Pass Under Heaven”.
Snowmelt from the Qilian Mountains, which rise above 5,000 m, waters the oases of the Hexi Corridor.

q.q: Jiayu Pass marks the western end of which Great Wall?

Q69060.t: A high valley city on the edge of the Tibetan Plateau
Q69060.s: Xining lies about 2,200 m up, stretched along the narrow valley of the Huangshui River between bare, deeply gullied hills. This is the threshold of the Tibetan Plateau: west of here the land climbs to Qinghai Lake and the high grasslands. For centuries the city was a market where Chinese tea was traded for Tibetan horses. Its name means “western peace”.
Q69060.w: A long city squeezed into a narrow valley between bare, eroded hills, with higher mountains to the west.
f: Kumbum Monastery, about 25 km south-west, marks the birthplace of Tsongkhapa, founder of the Gelug school.
Qinghai Lake, about 150 km to the west, is the largest lake in China.
The railway to Lhasa, crossing passes over 5,000 m high, begins its climb here.

q.q: Xining is the capital of which province?

Q189633.t: A city among limestone towers, on the 20-yuan note
Q189633.s: Guilin is scattered among hundreds of steep, rounded limestone towers rising straight out of flat green fields, and from above they look like a field of giant molehills. The Li River slips south between them towards Yangshuo, through one of the most painted landscapes in China. The name means “forest of sweet osmanthus”, after the trees that scent the city every autumn.
Q189633.w: A city among countless steep, rounded limestone peaks, with a river winding south between them through green fields.
f: A Li River scene near Guilin appears on the back of the 20-yuan banknote.
The Lingqu Canal, dug around 214 BC north of Guilin, is one of the oldest canals in the world.
A Chinese saying claims Guilin's scenery is the finest under heaven.

q.q: A Li River scene near Guilin appears on which banknote?

Q360178.t: Coal, tofu and solar panels floating on mine lakes
Q360178.s: Huainan stretches along the south bank of the Huai River, the traditional line between northern and southern China. Coal has been mined here for over a century, and where the ground has sunk above old workings it has flooded into shallow lakes; some now carry dark grids of floating solar panels. Legend credits Liu An, a prince of Huainan in the 2nd century BC, with inventing tofu.
Q360178.w: An industrial city along the south bank of a big river, with scattered lakes, some covered in dark grids of solar panels.
f: A battle at the nearby Fei River in 383 gave Chinese the idiom “every bush and tree looks like a soldier”.
Together with the Qinling Mountains, the Huai River is taken as the boundary between north and south China.

q.q: Legend credits a prince of Huainan with inventing which food?

Q59100.t: Teochew heartland on the delta of the Han River
Q59100.s: Shantou spreads over the flat delta of the Han River where it meets the South China Sea, wrapped around a sheltered harbour lagoon. The land nearby is a mosaic of fish ponds and paddies, and the big island of Nan'ao lies offshore to the east. This is the heart of Chaoshan, or Teochew, country, famous for its cooking and its elaborate gongfu tea ritual.
Q59100.w: A coastal city on a flat river delta around a sheltered harbour, fish ponds around it and a large island to the east.
f: In 1980 Shantou became one of China's first four Special Economic Zones.
Many Chinese communities in Thailand and across South-East Asia trace their roots to Teochew emigrants from this region.

q.q: What did Western traders call Shantou?

Q14501.t: An oil island among Borneo's mangrove deltas
Q14501.s: Tarakan sits on a small island just off the north-east coast of Borneo, where several rivers break into a maze of muddy channels and mangrove forest. From above, the island looks like a green patch ringed by brown water. Oil has been pumped here since the early 1900s, and its wells and refinery made the island a busy port of the Dutch East Indies.
Q14501.w: A small green island off a coast of muddy river channels and dark mangroves; the town on its south-western shore.
f: A mangrove reserve inside the city is home to proboscis monkeys, famous for their long noses.
Tarakan is the largest city of North Kalimantan, a province created in 2012.

q.q: Which long-nosed monkey lives in Tarakan's mangrove reserve?

Q11025.t: A port city climbing from the coast into volcanic hills
Q11025.s: Semarang has two levels: a flat lower town along the Java Sea coast and a greener upper town climbing the hills to the south, with the volcano Ungaran rising beyond. The old Dutch quarter near the harbour is nicknamed Little Netherlands. Local tradition says the Chinese admiral Zheng He landed here in the early 15th century, and the Sam Poo Kong temple honours him.
Q11025.w: A city on a flat coast that climbs onto green hills to the south; a volcano behind, a harbour in front.
f: Lawang Sewu, built in 1907 as a Dutch railway office, is called the “Thousand Doors” for its many doors and windows.
Semarang is the capital of Central Java.

q.q: Semarang's Sam Poo Kong temple honours which Chinese admiral?

Q8131.t: Srivijaya's old capital on the wide brown Musi
Q8131.s: Palembang straddles the broad, brown Musi River, far inland across the flat swamps and plantations of southern Sumatra. Ships still come upriver from the sea, a journey of close to 100 km. More than a thousand years ago this was the heart of Srivijaya, a maritime empire that controlled trade through the Strait of Malacca. Look for the long bridge joining the two halves of the city.
Q8131.w: A city on both banks of a wide brown river winding through flat swampy lowland, with a long bridge across.
f: The Ampera Bridge, opened in 1965, was built with a centre span that lifted for ships; it was later fixed in place.
Wooden houses floating on rafts still line parts of the riverbank.
The Chinese pilgrim Yijing studied Sanskrit in Srivijaya in the late 7th century.

q.q: Palembang was the heart of which maritime empire?

Q14182.t: The city of a thousand rivers and floating markets
Q14182.s: Banjarmasin lies in the flat, swampy lowlands of southern Borneo, where the Martapura River joins the wide Barito not far from the sea. Rivers and canals thread through every district, earning it the name City of a Thousand Rivers. At dawn, traders in small boats gather on the water for its famous floating markets, selling fruit and vegetables straight from their canoes.
Q14182.w: A flat city laced with rivers and canals beside a wide brown river, surrounded by swampy lowland and rice fields.
f: The Banjar Sultanate, founded in the 1520s, ruled from here for more than three centuries.
Much of the city lies barely above the level of high tide.

q.q: Banjarmasin is famous for its…

Q14634.t: A seafaring city facing a scatter of coral islands
Q14634.s: Makassar lines the flat west coast of South Sulawesi, looking out over the Spermonde Archipelago, a scatter of tiny coral islands ringed with turquoise reefs. Inland to the north-east rise the jagged limestone towers of Maros. For centuries this was the great trading port of the Gowa sultanate, and its sailors ranged across the eastern seas.
Q14634.w: A city on a flat coast facing dozens of tiny coral islands; jagged limestone hills inland to the north-east.
f: From the 18th century, Makassan sailors voyaged each year to northern Australia to gather sea cucumbers.
Fort Rotterdam in the city centre was rebuilt by the Dutch in the 1670s on the site of a Gowa fortress.

q.q: Makassan sailors once voyaged to northern Australia to collect…

Q5869.t: A city in a high Himalayan valley, 3,650 m up
Q5869.s: Lhasa lies in the flat valley of the Kyi Chu, a tributary of the Yarlung Tsangpo, about 3,650 m above sea level — and even so, the bare brown mountains around it rise another 1,500 m or more. The air is thin and dry, and sunshine is so plentiful that Lhasa is nicknamed the City of Sunlight. Its name means “place of the gods”.
Q5869.w: A green, flat-floored river valley hemmed in by steep bare mountains, with the city spread along its northern side.
f: The Potala Palace, on a hill in the city, rises 13 storeys and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The Jokhang Temple in the old centre dates back to the 7th century.
Lhasa gets about 3,000 hours of sunshine a year.

q.q: Roughly how high above sea level does Lhasa lie?

Q650585.t: The melon oasis at the eastern end of the Tian Shan
Q650585.s: Hami is a green oasis at the southern foot of the Karlik Mountains, the snowy eastern tail of the Tian Shan, with vast gravel desert stretching away on every side. For Silk Road caravans coming from Gansu, this was the first great oasis after days of crossing the Gobi. Its name travels the world on the famous Hami melon, sweet and crisp.
Q650585.w: A green oasis at the foot of snowy mountains, surrounded by vast grey gravel desert; large solar farms nearby.
f: Hami melons were sent as tribute to the Qing emperors from the late 17th century.
Its central district, Yizhou, carries the oasis's Tang-era name; in Uyghur the oasis is called Kumul.

q.q: Which fruit is named after Hami?

Q235389.t: A jade oasis on the edge of the Taklamakan
Q235389.s: Hotan is a green oasis squeezed between the snowy Kunlun Mountains to the south and the sand sea of the Taklamakan to the north. Two braided rivers, the White Jade and the Black Jade, run down from the mountains on either side of it, then join and push north into the desert. For thousands of years people have picked nephrite jade from their gravel beds.
Q235389.w: A green oasis between two braided rivers, snowy mountains to the south and an endless sea of dunes to the north.
f: Hotan jade was carried east to the courts of China's rulers for thousands of years.
A legend recorded by the monk Xuanzang says silk reached Khotan when a princess hid silkworm eggs in her headdress.
The Hotan River crosses the Taklamakan only in summer, when snowmelt fills it.

q.q: Which stone is found in the rivers of Hotan?

Q170521.t: A Silk Road crossroads at the foot of the Pamirs
Q170521.s: Kashgar is a green oasis at the far western tip of the Tarim Basin, where the Tian Shan, the Pamirs and the Kunlun close in around the desert. For caravans it was the great junction: routes skirting the Taklamakan to north and south met here before climbing to the high passes westward. On clear days, the snow domes of Kongur and Muztagh Ata, both over 7,500 m, rise to the south-west.
Q170521.w: A green oasis at the western end of a desert basin, walls of snowy mountains rising to the west, north and south.
f: Mahmud al-Kashgari, from this region, compiled the first great dictionary of the Turkic languages in the 1070s.
Kashgar's Sunday livestock market has drawn traders from across the region for generations.

q.q: Which 11th-century scholar from here compiled a great Turkic dictionary?

Q211243.t: A green plain between a mountain wall and the Yellow River
Q211243.s: Yinchuan lies on a strip of green, irrigated plain between the dark, jagged Helan Mountains to the west and the Yellow River to the east. The mountains shield it from the sands of the Tengger Desert, and canals first dug over 2,000 years ago spread the river's water across the fields. Its lakes and paddies earned the area the name “Jiangnan beyond the frontier”.
Q211243.w: A green, lake-dotted plain between a long, dark mountain range to the west and a broad river to the east; desert beyond.
f: From the 11th to the 13th century Yinchuan was the capital of the Western Xia kingdom.
The royal tombs of the Western Xia stand at the foot of the Helan Mountains, west of the city.
Ningxia's goji berries are famous across China.

q.q: Yinchuan was the capital of which medieval kingdom?

Q362865.t: An old coal town in the hills of the Hunan border
Q362865.s: Pingxiang sits in a valley of green hills on Jiangxi's western border, where the Luoxiao Mountains divide the province from Hunan. Its fortunes were built on coal: the Anyuan mine, opened in 1898, fed one of China's first modern ironworks. To the south-east rises Wugong Mountain, whose rounded summits are covered in grassland rather than forest.
Q362865.w: A city in a valley among green, rolling hills, with higher mountains along the border to the west and south.
f: Coke from Anyuan fed the Hanyang Iron Works in Wuhan, one of China's first modern steel plants.
Wugong Mountain's summit grasslands, over 1,900 m up, turn golden in autumn.

q.q: What did Pingxiang's Anyuan mine, opened in 1898, produce?

Q38234.t: Japan's window to Europe, round a narrow harbour
Q38234.s: Nagasaki wraps around a long, narrow harbour, with houses climbing steep green hills on both sides like the seats of an amphitheatre. Portuguese ships made it a port in 1571. For more than two centuries of Japan's isolation, a small artificial island here, Dejima, was the country's only regular window to Europe. Offshore to the south-west lies a scatter of islands.
Q38234.w: A long, narrow harbour like a fjord, the city climbing steep green hills on both sides; islands to the south-west.
f: From 1641 to 1859, Dutch traders on Dejima were the only Europeans allowed to trade with Japan.
Castella, a sponge cake still sold all over Nagasaki, arrived with Portuguese traders in the 16th century.

q.q: Which Europeans traded at Dejima from 1641?

Q205922.t: The crane city on the marshes of the Nen River
Q205922.s: Qiqihar spreads across the flat Songnen Plain beside the Nen River, in a landscape of reed marshes and shallow lakes that shine like scattered mirrors. South-east of the city lies Zhalong, a vast wetland where red-crowned cranes nest in summer; it became one of China's first nature reserves for cranes. The town began as a Qing fortress in 1691.
Q205922.w: A city beside a braided river on a flat plain of reed marsh and shallow lakes; white and frozen in winter.
f: Zhalong's reed marshes cover more than 2,000 km².
In Chinese art, the red-crowned crane is a symbol of long life.

q.q: Which bird is Zhalong wetland near Qiqihar famous for?

Q200016.t: Where the Eastern Ghats run down to the Bay of Bengal
Q200016.s: Visakhapatnam, or Vizag, sits where green hills of the Eastern Ghats come right down to the Bay of Bengal. Its deep harbour is tucked behind a rocky headland called Dolphin's Nose, and long sandy beaches curve away to the north. The city is named after Visakha, a Hindu god of valour. Inland, the hills climb towards the Araku Valley and its coffee plantations.
Q200016.w: A coastal city between green hills and the sea, a harbour behind a rocky headland, long beaches to the north.
f: Visakhapatnam is one of India's largest ports.
Coffee from the Araku Valley, grown largely by tribal farmers, has become known worldwide.

q.q: Vizag's harbour is sheltered by a headland called…

Q38807.t: A rainy harbour capital ringed by coral reefs
Q38807.s: Suva sits on a hilly peninsula on the south-east coast of Viti Levu, Fiji's main island, between a deep harbour and Laucala Bay. Look for the pale line of surf on the reef offshore and dark, rain-soaked mountains behind the city — clouds gather here often, and it is far wetter than Fiji's western side. Suva replaced Levuka as the capital in 1882.
Q38807.w: A city on a hilly peninsula between two bays, a pale line of reef offshore, green cloud-capped mountains behind.
f: Suva gets around 3,000 mm of rain a year — several times as much as London.
Levuka, the old capital on the island of Ovalau, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

q.q: Which town was Fiji's capital before Suva?

Q1520.t: A capital of many names on the open steppe
Q1520.s: This city rises from a flat, almost treeless steppe on the banks of the winding Ishim River, and in winter everything around it turns white under a hard frost. It began as the fort of Akmolinsk in 1830 and has changed its name more often than almost any capital: Tselinograd, Akmola, Astana, Nur-Sultan and, since 2022, Astana again. Kazakhstan moved its capital here from Almaty in 1997.
Q1520.w: A compact city on a flat, treeless steppe, with a winding river through it; white and frozen in winter.
f: Winter nights here often drop below −30 °C, making it one of the coldest capitals in the world.
The Ishim flows on north into Russia, where it joins the Irtysh.

q.q: What was the city called from 1961 to 1992?

Q484706.t: A coal city on the steppe, named after a shrub
Q484706.s: Qaraghandy, better known as Karaganda, sprawls across the bare Kazakh steppe, and around it you can spot the cones of old spoil heaps left by its coal mines. Coal was found here in 1833 — by a shepherd boy, local tradition says — and the modern city grew fast from the 1930s. Its name comes from karagan, the hardy caragana shrub that grows across the steppe.
Q484706.w: A sprawling city on flat, bare steppe, dotted with conical spoil heaps; a steel town and reservoir to the north-west.
f: The Karaganda coal basin is one of the largest in Central Asia.
The steel town of Temirtau, about 30 km north-west, grew up beside a reservoir on the Nura River.

q.q: Karaganda is named after which steppe plant?

Q35493.t: The apple city beneath a wall of snowy peaks
Q35493.s: Almaty spreads across a gently sloping plain at the very foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau, whose snowy peaks rise to nearly 5,000 m just south of the city — a wall of white hanging over the rooftops. The forests on these slopes are home to the wild apple from which the world's cultivated apples descend, and the city's name recalls the fruit.
Q35493.w: A big city on a slope running up to a steep wall of snowy mountains to the south; flat steppe to the north.
f: The city began in 1854 as the Russian fort of Verny.
Almaty was the capital of Kazakhstan until 1997.
Medeu, a skating rink in a gorge above the city, lies at about 1,700 m.

q.q: Wild apples in the mountains near Almaty are the ancestors of…

Q48403.t: The city of the Golden Temple and its pool of nectar
Q48403.s: Amritsar lies on the flat, fertile plain of Punjab, surrounded by a patchwork of wheat and rice fields laced with canals. Its heart is the Golden Temple, the holiest shrine of the Sikh faith, standing in the middle of a sacred pool. The city grew up around that pool in the 1570s under Guru Ram Das, and its name means “pool of nectar”.
Q48403.w: A dense city on a flat green plain of fields and canals stretching to the horizon in every direction.
f: The Golden Temple's community kitchen serves free meals to tens of thousands of visitors every day.
The temple's upper storeys were covered in gold leaf in the early 19th century under Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

q.q: What does the name Amritsar mean?

Q79980.t: A holy city on a crescent bend of the Ganges
Q79980.s: Varanasi lines the west bank of the Ganges where the river curves in a great crescent and, unusually, flows northwards. The contrast is striking from above: the city packs the western shore with stone steps, or ghats, while the eastern bank stays an almost empty strip of sand. It is often called one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
Q79980.w: A dense city on the west side of a crescent-shaped bend of a wide river, with a bare sandy bank opposite.
f: At Sarnath, about 10 km north-east, the Buddha is said to have given his first sermon.
More than 80 ghats line the river for several kilometres.

q.q: Who gave his first sermon at Sarnath, near Varanasi?

Q202139.t: Where India first dug for coal
Q202139.s: Asansol spreads over rolling red-earth country between the Damodar and Ajay rivers, on the edge of the Chota Nagpur Plateau. This is the Raniganj coalfield, where commercial coal mining in India began in 1774, and the land around is dotted with pits, spoil heaps and flooded workings. To the west, dams on the Damodar and Barakar hold back large reservoirs.
Q202139.w: An industrial city on rolling reddish land dotted with pits and ponds, a river to the south, reservoirs to the west.
f: The Damodar was once called the “Sorrow of Bengal” for its floods, until dams were built on it in the 1950s.
The Grand Trunk Road, one of Asia's oldest highways, runs through the city.

q.q: When did commercial coal mining in India begin, in the Raniganj field?

Q242144.t: A steel town built with Soviet help on a rice plain
Q242144.s: Bhilai rose in the 1950s around one of India's largest steelworks, built with Soviet help on the flat plain of Chhattisgarh. From above, look for the vast grey rectangle of the plant with its cooling ponds, and a neatly planned town beside it. All around stretches a quilt of paddy fields: Chhattisgarh is often called the rice bowl of India.
Q242144.w: A huge grey industrial complex with ponds beside a planned town, set in a flat patchwork of green paddy fields.
f: The Bhilai plant has long been India's main maker of steel rails.
Bhilai and neighbouring Durg have grown together into a single urban area.

q.q: Bhilai's steelworks was built in the 1950s with help from…

Q80989.t: The city of lakes, once ruled by queens
Q80989.s: Bhopal wraps around two large lakes on the hilly Malwa Plateau, and the bigger one, the Upper Lake, dominates the view from above. Tradition says Raja Bhoj created it in the 11th century by damming a river. For more than a century from 1819, Bhopal was ruled by a line of four women, the Begums — a rarity in Indian history.
Q80989.w: A city on low hills around two large lakes, the western one much bigger; plateau and farmland all around.
f: The Buddhist stupa of Sanchi, a UNESCO site, lies about 45 km to the north-east.
The rock shelters of Bhimbetka, south-east of the city, hold paintings thousands of years old.

q.q: Bhopal's Upper Lake is traditionally credited to which king?

Q228405.t: Temple city of the Tamils, among granite hills
Q228405.s: Madurai spreads along the Vaigai River on a flat plain studded with bare granite hills; one, Yanaimalai, is said to look like a resting elephant. At the city's heart stands the Meenakshi Temple, whose colourful gateway towers rise above the streets. Madurai has been a centre of Tamil culture for over two thousand years, and tradition places the ancient Tamil poets' academies here.
Q228405.w: A city on a sandy river amid a flat plain dotted with isolated bare rocky hills, one long and elephant-shaped.
f: The Meenakshi Temple has 14 gateway towers; the tallest is about 50 m high.
Madurai's jasmine is so prized that it carries a geographical indication tag.

q.q: Madurai's great temple is dedicated to the goddess…

Q9885.t: A mill city by the great gap in the Western Ghats
Q9885.s: Coimbatore sits on a plain hemmed in by mountains: the Nilgiri Hills rise steeply to the north, and the Western Ghats wall off the west — except for the Palakkad Gap, a break some 30–40 km wide that lets winds and roads through to Kerala. Its many cotton mills earned the city the nickname Manchester of South India.
Q9885.w: A large city on a plain, a massive mountain block to the north, steep ranges to the west with a wide gap in them.
f: The Palakkad Gap is the main break in the Western Ghats, which otherwise run unbroken for over 1,000 km.
Coimbatore is famous across India for its wet grinders, which carry a geographical indication tag.

q.q: Which gap in the Western Ghats lies just west of Coimbatore?

Q9326.t: A low, leafy capital on a great bend of the Mekong
Q9326.s: Vientiane lies low and leafy along a broad bend of the Mekong, and across the water you are looking at Thailand. In the dry season the river shrinks to reveal long sandbars. King Setthathirath moved the capital of the Lan Xang kingdom here from Luang Prabang in 1560. The name is usually translated as “city of sandalwood”.
Q9326.w: A low, green city along a wide river bend with sandbars; the far bank belongs to another country.
f: The golden stupa of Pha That Luang is the national symbol of Laos.
The first Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge, opened in 1994, crosses the Mekong just downstream.

q.q: King Setthathirath moved his capital to Vientiane in 1560 from…

Q9279.t: A riverside capital with a whole village on stilts
Q9279.s: Bandar Seri Begawan sits on the Brunei River a few kilometres from Brunei Bay, surrounded by dark green rainforest. Across the river from the centre spreads Kampong Ayer, a village of houses on stilts linked by boardwalks — one of the largest water villages in the world. In 1521 members of Magellan's expedition visited and marvelled at a town built over the water.
Q9279.w: A small city on a river winding through rainforest, a large cluster of stilt houses on the water, a long bridge across the bay.
f: The Temburong Bridge, opened in 2020, runs about 30 km across Brunei Bay to the country's separate eastern part.
The city took its present name in 1970; before that it was called Brunei Town.

q.q: What is Kampong Ayer?
q.a: A village on stilts over water

Q45604.t: A pomegranate oasis between bare ridges and red sands
Q45604.s: Kandahar lies on a dry plain about 1,000 m up, with bare, jagged ridges rising around it and the reddish dunes of the Registan Desert spreading to the south. North-west of the city, the Arghandab River feeds a ribbon of green orchards famous for pomegranates. In 1747 Ahmad Shah Durrani made Kandahar the capital of his new empire, and he is buried here.
Q45604.w: A city on a dry brown plain among bare rocky ridges, with a green ribbon of orchards along a river to the north-west.
f: Many historians link Kandahar with a city founded by Alexander the Great, Alexandria in Arachosia.
Kandahar's pomegranates are prized across the region.

q.q: The Arghandab valley near Kandahar is famous for which fruit?

Q1850.t: A capital where four river arms meet
Q1850.s: Phnom Penh stands at a great watery crossroads called Chaktomuk, “four faces”: the Mekong, the Tonle Sap and the Bassac meet here in an X of brown water. Each rainy season the Mekong swells so much that the Tonle Sap River reverses and flows backwards, filling the great lake upstream. The city's name means “hill of Penh”, after a woman who, legend says, founded a shrine here.
Q1850.w: A city at an X-shaped meeting of wide brown rivers, surrounded by flat floodplain and paddies.
f: In the wet season Tonle Sap Lake can grow to several times its dry-season size.
King Norodom moved the royal capital here from Oudong in 1866.

q.q: What does the Tonle Sap River do each rainy season?
